treeio

Top-level package for treeio.

A pure-Python library for reading, writing, manipulating and plotting phylogenetic trees. The core engine works on the standard library alone; plotting uses matplotlib (imported lazily on first draw).

class Tree: 
  47class Tree:
  48    """
  49    Tree class is used to store a tree object.
  50
  51                  ┌ Theta
  52          ┌─ Beta ┤
  53    Alpha ┤       └ Delta
  54          │
  55          └ Gamma
  56    """
  57
  58    # first-class slots (``__slots__`` keeps per-node memory small); arbitrary
  59    # annotation attributes are consolidated into a single lazy ``_annotations``
  60    # dict instead of scattering extra keys into each node's ``__dict__``.
  61    __slots__ = (
  62        "__weakref__",
  63        "_annotations",
  64        "_children",
  65        "_parent",
  66        "branch_length",
  67        "name",
  68        "support",
  69    )
  70
  71    # slots that are treated as first-class attributes.
  72    _SLOTS = ("name", "branch_length", "support", "_parent", "_children")
  73
  74    def __init__(self, name="unknown", branch_length=None, support=None, **kwargs):
  75        """Create a node.
  76
  77        Each argument is stored as an attribute on the node.  ``branch_length``
  78        is the branch length leading to this node (``None`` if unknown) and
  79        ``support`` the support / bootstrap value (``None`` if unknown).
  80
  81        Keyword arguments become arbitrary per-node annotations (stored in a
  82        single dict).  If ``parent`` is supplied the node is attached
  83        underneath it.
  84        """
  85        object.__setattr__(self, "name", name)
  86        object.__setattr__(self, "branch_length", branch_length)
  87        object.__setattr__(self, "support", support)
  88        object.__setattr__(self, "_parent", None)
  89        object.__setattr__(self, "_children", [])
  90        object.__setattr__(self, "_annotations", None)
  91
  92        # support any value, attached as annotation.
  93        for key, value in kwargs.items():
  94            if key == "parent":
  95                self.parent = value
  96            else:
  97                setattr(self, key, value)
  98
  99    def __setattr__(self, name: str, value) -> None:
 100        """Store slots / properties directly; everything else in ``_annotations``."""
 101        try:
 102            object.__setattr__(self, name, value)
 103        except AttributeError:
 104            ann = object.__getattribute__(self, "_annotations")
 105            if ann is None:
 106                ann = {}
 107                object.__setattr__(self, "_annotations", ann)
 108            ann[name] = value
 109
 110    def __getattr__(self, name: str):
 111        """Look up annotation attributes stored in ``_annotations``."""
 112        ann = object.__getattribute__(self, "_annotations")
 113        if ann is not None and name in ann:
 114            return ann[name]
 115        raise AttributeError(name)
 116
 117    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 118    # iteration / string
 119    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 120    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[Tree]:
 121        """Iterate over all descendant nodes (post-order), self last."""
 122        stack = [(self, False)]
 123        while stack:
 124            node, visited = stack.pop()
 125            if visited:
 126                yield node
 127            else:
 128                stack.append((node, True))
 129                # push children in reverse so they are yielded left-to-right
 130                for ch in reversed(node._children):
 131                    stack.append((ch, False))
 132
 133    def __len__(self) -> int:
 134        """Number of nodes that are descendants of (and including) self."""
 135        count = 0
 136        stack = [self]
 137        while stack:
 138            node = stack.pop()
 139            count += 1
 140            stack.extend(node._children)
 141        return count
 142
 143    def __contains__(self, node) -> bool:
 144        """``node in tree`` is true when ``node`` is a descendant of ``self``."""
 145        return self.is_ancestor_of(node)
 146
 147    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
 148        return True
 149
 150    def __repr__(self) -> str:
 151        return f"<Tree: {self.name}>"
 152
 153    def __str__(self) -> str:
 154        """Print tree in console by ascii art."""
 155        from .show import tree_to_ascii
 156
 157        return tree_to_ascii(self, False, True)
 158
 159    def __eq__(self, other) -> bool:
 160        if not isinstance(other, Tree):
 161            return NotImplemented
 162        stack = [(self, other)]
 163        while stack:
 164            a, b = stack.pop()
 165            if (
 166                a.name != b.name
 167                or a.branch_length != b.branch_length
 168                or a.support != b.support
 169            ):
 170                return False
 171            if len(a._children) != len(b._children):
 172                return False
 173            stack.extend(zip(a._children, b._children))
 174        return True
 175
 176    def __hash__(self) -> int:  # used by set/dict if hashing needed
 177        return id(self)
 178
 179    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 180    # parent / children
 181    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 182    @property
 183    def parent(self) -> Tree | None:
 184        """Get the parent of tree node."""
 185        return self._parent
 186
 187    @parent.setter
 188    def parent(self, value: Tree | None) -> None:
 189        if value is None:
 190            self._detach_from_parent()
 191            return
 192        if isinstance(value, type(self)):
 193            if self._parent is not None and self._parent is not value:
 194                self._detach_from_parent()
 195            self._parent = value
 196            if not any(c is self for c in value._children):
 197                value._children.append(self)
 198        else:
 199            raise TypeError("parent must be a Tree or None")
 200
 201    @parent.deleter
 202    def parent(self) -> None:
 203        self._detach_from_parent()
 204
 205    def _detach_from_parent(self) -> None:
 206        """Remove self from the current parent's children (keeps graph consistent)."""
 207        p = self._parent
 208        self._parent = None
 209        if p is not None:
 210            p._children = [c for c in p._children if c is not self]
 211
 212    @property
 213    def children(self) -> _ChildrenView:
 214        """Read-only view of the children (use :meth:`append_child` to mutate)."""
 215        return _ChildrenView(self._children)
 216
 217    @children.setter
 218    def children(self, value: Iterable[Tree]) -> None:
 219        if hasattr(value, "__iter__") and all(isinstance(n, type(self)) for n in value):
 220            # Detach any previously-attached children that are being replaced so
 221            # their stale ``_parent`` pointers do not linger.
 222            for old in self._children:
 223                old._parent = None
 224            self._children = []
 225            for node in value:
 226                self.append_child(node)
 227        else:
 228            raise ValueError("children must be an iterable of Tree nodes")
 229
 230    @children.deleter
 231    def children(self) -> None:
 232        for c in list(self._children):
 233            c._parent = None
 234        self._children = []
 235
 236    def append_child(self, tree: Tree):
 237        """Add a child node (detaching it from any previous parent)."""
 238        if tree is self:
 239            raise ValueError("cannot attach a node to itself")
 240        if any(c is tree for c in self._children):
 241            return self
 242        if tree._parent is not None:
 243            tree._detach_from_parent()
 244        tree._parent = self
 245        self._children.append(tree)
 246        return self
 247
 248    def extend_children(self, tree: Iterable[Tree]):
 249        """Add several children and return self."""
 250        for t in tree:
 251            self.append_child(t)
 252        return self
 253
 254    def remove_child(self, tree: Tree):
 255        """Detach ``tree`` from ``self``.
 256
 257        Raises ``ValueError`` if ``tree`` is not a direct child of ``self``.
 258        """
 259        if not any(c is tree for c in self._children):
 260            raise ValueError("The input node is not a child node.")
 261        tree._parent = None
 262        self._children = [c for c in self._children if c is not tree]
 263        return self
 264
 265    def isolated(self) -> Tree:
 266        """Isolate tree, turn into root node."""
 267        self._detach_from_parent()
 268        return self
 269
 270    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 271    # topology queries
 272    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 273    def is_leaf(self) -> bool:
 274        """Check node is a leaf (terminal node) or not."""
 275        return len(self.children) == 0
 276
 277    def is_root(self) -> bool:
 278        """Check node is a root (starting node) or not."""
 279        return self.parent is None
 280
 281    def is_internal(self) -> bool:
 282        """Check node is an internal (non-terminal, non-root) node."""
 283        return not self.is_leaf()
 284
 285    def is_binary(self) -> bool:
 286        """Check the (sub)tree is fully bifurcating (no multifurcation).
 287
 288        Implemented iteratively (explicit stack) so it copes with very deep
 289        trees without hitting the recursion limit.
 290        """
 291        stack = [self]
 292        while stack:
 293            node = stack.pop()
 294            if node.is_leaf():
 295                continue
 296            if len(node._children) != 2:
 297                return False
 298            stack.extend(node._children)
 299        return True
 300
 301    # alias used by toytree / ete3
 302    is_bifurcating = is_binary
 303
 304    def is_rooted(self) -> bool:
 305        """Return whether this tree is rooted.
 306
 307        Trees default to rooted ``True``.  :meth:`unroot` and the PhyloXML
 308        reader (via its ``rooted`` attribute) record an unrooted state in the
 309        ``_is_rooted`` annotation, which is reflected here.
 310        """
 311        return getattr(self, "_is_rooted", True)
 312
 313    def get_tips(self) -> list[Tree]:
 314        """Return leaf nodes (terminal taxa) in depth-first order."""
 315        return [n for n in self if n.is_leaf()]

 317    get_leaves = get_tips

 319    def get_internal_nodes(self) -> list[Tree]:

 378    def is_monophyletic(self, *names) -> bool:
 379        """Return ``True`` if *all* ``names`` form a single clade."""
 380        tips = {n.name for n in self.get_tips()}
 381        target = set(names)
 382        if not target <= tips:
 383            return False
 384        # find node containing exactly target
 385        for node in self.get_nodes():
 386            below = {n.name for n in node.get_tips()}
 387            if below == target:
 388                return True
 389        return False
 390
 391    def is_outgroup(self, *names) -> bool:
 392        """True when the clade of ``names`` is sibling to everything else."""
 393        tips = {n.name for n in self.get_tips()}
 394        target = set(names)
 395        if not target <= tips:
 396            return False
 397        # an outgroup splits the root into exactly two children
 398        if len(self.children) != 2:
 399            return False
 400        for c in self.children:
 401            if {n.name for n in c.get_tips()} == target:
 402                return True
 403        return False
 404
 405    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 406    # traversal (iterators)
 407    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 408    def traverse(self, order: str = "preorder") -> Iterator[Tree]:
 409        """Iterate over descendant nodes.
 410
 411        order: one of ``'preorder'``, ``'postorder'``, ``'levelorder'``.
 412        The node ``self`` is included.  (Iterative, so it copes with very
 413        deep trees without hitting the recursion limit.)
 414        """
 415        if order == "postorder":
 416            stack = [(self, False)]
 417            while stack:
 418                node, visited = stack.pop()
 419                if visited:
 420                    yield node
 421                else:
 422                    stack.append((node, True))
 423                    for ch in reversed(node._children):
 424                        stack.append((ch, False))
 425        elif order == "levelorder":
 426            frontier = [self]
 427            while frontier:
 428                nxt = []
 429                for node in frontier:
 430                    yield node
 431                    nxt.extend(node._children)
 432                frontier = nxt
 433        elif order == "preorder":
 434            stack = [self]
 435            while stack:
 436                node = stack.pop()
 437                yield node
 438                # push children in reverse so they are visited left-to-right
 439                for ch in reversed(node._children):
 440                    stack.append(ch)
 441        else:
 442            raise ValueError(f"unknown order {order!r}")
 443
 444    def is_ancestor_of(self, node: Tree) -> bool:
 445        """Return ``True`` if ``node`` is ``self`` or a descendant of ``self``."""
 446        cur = node
 447        while cur is not None:
 448            if cur is self:
 449                return True
 450            cur = cur._parent
 451        return False
 452
 453    def walk(self, order: str = "preorder") -> Iterator[Tree]:
 454        """Alias of :meth:`traverse`."""
 455        return self.traverse(order)
 456
 457    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 458    # search / ancestry
 459    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 460    def label_index(self) -> dict[str, Tree]:
 461        """Build ``{node_name: node}`` (first occurrence wins) in one pass.
 462
 463        Use this for bulk label lookups (e.g. data attachment) instead of
 464        calling :meth:`get_node_by_label` repeatedly.
 465        """
 466        index: dict[str, Tree] = {}
 467        for node in self.traverse("preorder"):
 468            name = node.name
 469            if name not in index:
 470                index[name] = node
 471        return index
 472
 473    def get_node_by_label(self, name: str) -> Tree | None:
 474        """Return the (first) node whose ``name`` equals ``name``."""
 475        for n in self:
 476            if n.name == name:
 477                return n
 478        return None
 479
 480    def get_tip_by_label(self, name: str) -> Tree | None:
 481        """Return the tip whose label equals ``name``."""
 482        for n in self.get_tips():
 483            if n.name == name:
 484                return n
 485        return None
 486
 487    def get_ancestors(self, node: Tree) -> list[Tree]:
 488        """Return the chain of ancestors from ``node`` up to the root."""
 489        out, cur = [], node
 490        while cur is not None and cur is not self:
 491            out.append(cur)
 492            cur = cur.parent
 493        if cur is not None:
 494            out.append(self)
 495        return out
 496
 497    def get_ancestors_of(self, node: Tree) -> list[Tree]:
 498        """Alias of :meth:`get_ancestors` (own ancestors, not including node)."""
 499        out, cur = [], node.parent
 500        while cur is not None:
 501            out.append(cur)
 502            cur = cur.parent
 503        return out
 504
 505    def get_descendants(self, node: Tree) -> list[Tree]:
 506        """Return all strict descendants of ``node`` (excluding ``node``)."""
 507        return [n for n in node if n is not node]
 508
 509    def get_nodes_below(self, node: Tree) -> list[Tree]:
 510        """Return the clade rooted at ``node`` (including it)."""
 511        return list(node)
 512
 513    def get_common_ancestor(self, node1: Tree, node2: Tree) -> Tree | None:
 514        """Return the most recent common ancestor of two nodes.
 515
 516        Uses a depth-based walk from the shared root, so it avoids the
 517        per-call ancestor-set allocation and is safe for very deep trees.
 518        """
 519        return self._lca_node(node1, node2)
 520
 521    def get_mrca(self, *nodes) -> Tree | None:
 522        """Return the most recent common ancestor of a set of nodes.
 523
 524        Accepts ``Tree`` nodes or names (strings).
 525        """
 526        resolved = [
 527            n if isinstance(n, Tree) else self.get_node_by_label(n) for n in nodes
 528        ]
 529        if not resolved or any(n is None for n in resolved):
 530            return None
 531        out = resolved[0]
 532        for n in resolved[1:]:
 533            out = self.get_common_ancestor(out, n)
 534        return out
 535
 536    # "mrca" as a method alias, following toytree/ete3 naming
 537    mrca = get_mrca
 538
 539    def _lca_node(self, node1: Tree, node2: Tree) -> Tree | None:
 540        """Lowest common ancestor of two nodes, or ``None`` if they belong to
 541        different trees (different root ancestors).
 542
 543        Depth is the number of ancestor edges from each node's own forest root
 544        (the highest ancestor).  Both nodes are brought to equal depth and then
 545        walked up together, giving the LCA in ``O(depth)`` with no per-call
 546        set/list allocation.  This yields exactly the same LCA the old
 547        set-based ``_ancestor_set`` approach produced.
 548        """
 549        d1 = 0
 550        n = node1
 551        while n._parent is not None:
 552            d1 += 1
 553            n = n._parent
 554        root1 = n
 555
 556        d2 = 0
 557        n = node2
 558        while n._parent is not None:
 559            d2 += 1
 560            n = n._parent
 561        root2 = n
 562
 563        if root1 is not root2:
 564            return None
 565
 566        x, y = node1, node2
 567        while d1 > d2:
 568            x = x._parent
 569            d1 -= 1
 570        while d2 > d1:
 571            y = y._parent
 572            d2 -= 1
 573        while x is not y:
 574            x = x._parent
 575            y = y._parent
 576        return x
 577
 578    def _node_depth_map(self) -> dict[Tree, int]:
 579        """Return ``{node: edge_depth}`` for every descendant of ``self``.
 580
 581        ``edge_depth`` is the number of ancestor edges from ``self`` (the root
 582        of this (sub)tree).  Built with an explicit stack so it copes with very
 583        deep trees without overflowing the recursion limit.
 584        """
 585        depth_map = {self: 0}
 586        stack = [self]
 587        while stack:
 588            node = stack.pop()
 589            nd = depth_map[node] + 1
 590            for c in node._children:
 591                depth_map[c] = nd
 592                stack.append(c)
 593        return depth_map
 594
 595    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 596    # distances
 597    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 598    def get_distance(self, node1: Tree, node2: Tree) -> float:
 599        """Return the patristic distance between two nodes.
 600
 601        Branch lengths are summed along the path; missing (``None``) branch
 602        lengths are treated as 0.
 603        """
 604        if not isinstance(node1, Tree) or not isinstance(node2, Tree):
 605            raise TypeError("get_distance expects Tree nodes")
 606
 607        lca = self._lca_node(node1, node2)
 608        if lca is None:
 609            raise ValueError("nodes are not in the same tree")
 610
 611        d = 0.0
 612        cur = node1
 613        while cur is not lca:
 614            bl = cur.branch_length
 615            d += 0.0 if bl is None else float(bl)
 616            cur = cur._parent
 617        cur = node2
 618        while cur is not lca:
 619            bl = cur.branch_length
 620            d += 0.0 if bl is None else float(bl)
 621            cur = cur._parent
 622        return d
 623
 624    def get_cophenetic_distance(self) -> list[list[float]]:
 625        """Return the pairwise patristic distance matrix for all tips.
 626
 627        Uses ``dist(a, b) = D(a) + D(b) - 2*D(mrca(a, b))`` where ``D(x)`` is
 628        the *branch-length* distance from the root down to ``x``.  ``D`` is
 629        computed once in a single traversal, then the ``n x n`` matrix is filled
 630        with numpy so the pairwise loop runs in C instead of Python (no per-pair
 631        Python LCA walk).  Every tip pair is written exactly once -- at its most
 632        recent common ancestor -- by filling the cross-clade block between each
 633        pair of children of that node; deeper clades already hold their own
 634        within-clade values.  This is ``O(n^2)`` element work for any shape.
 635        Iterative (explicit stacks), so it copes with very deep trees without
 636        hitting the recursion limit.
 637        """
 638        import math
 639
 640        tips = self.get_tips()
 641        n = len(tips)
 642        if n < 2:
 643            return [[0.0] * n for _ in range(n)]
 644
 645        import numpy as np
 646
 647        # Pre-order sweep: assign tip indices (contiguous per clade) and the
 648        # branch-length distance D from the root down to every node.
 649        nodes = []
 650        droot = {}
 651        tip_index = {}
 652        tip_counter = 0
 653        finite = True
 654        max_bl = 0.0
 655        min_pos_bl = None
 656        stack = [(self, 0.0)]
 657        while stack:
 658            node, parent_d = stack.pop()
 659            bl = node.branch_length
 660            if bl is not None:
 661                fb = abs(float(bl))
 662                max_bl = max(max_bl, fb)
 663                if fb and (min_pos_bl is None or fb < min_pos_bl):
 664                    min_pos_bl = fb
 665            d = parent_d + (0.0 if bl is None else float(bl))
 666            if finite and not math.isfinite(d):
 667                finite = False
 668            droot[node] = d
 669            nodes.append(node)
 670            if node.is_leaf():
 671                tip_index[node] = tip_counter
 672                tip_counter += 1
 673            for c in reversed(node._children):
 674                stack.append((c, d))
 675
 676        # ``inf`` / ``nan`` branch lengths break the ``D(a)+D(b)-2*D(lca)``
 677        # identity (``inf - inf`` is ``nan``), so fall back to the exact
 678        # per-pair path sum for such (pathological) trees.  ``get_distance``
 679        # reproduces the original LCA + summation result bit for bit.
 680        #
 681        # The same identity also suffers catastrophic cancellation when branch
 682        # lengths span a huge dynamic range (e.g. a 1e15 edge next to a 1e-3
 683        # tip edge): the tip values are lost in ``D`` and the result collapses
 684        # to 0 even though ``get_distance`` is correct.  Treat that as the same
 685        # non-finite/ill-conditioned case so the exact per-pair path sum is
 686        # used instead.
 687        if max_bl and min_pos_bl and min_pos_bl < max_bl * 2.0**-40:
 688            finite = False
 689        if not finite:
 690            mat = [[0.0] * n for _ in range(n)]
 691            for i in range(n):
 692                a = tips[i]
 693                for j in range(i + 1, n):
 694                    d = self.get_distance(a, tips[j])
 695                    mat[i][j] = mat[j][i] = d
 696            return mat
 697
 698        # Post-order pass records the contiguous tip-index range [lo, hi) that
 699        # each node's clade occupies (used as the numpy block to fill).
 700        lo = {}
 701        hi = {}
 702        stack = [(self, False)]
 703        while stack:
 704            node, visited = stack.pop()
 705            if visited:
 706                if node.is_leaf():
 707                    lo[node] = tip_index[node]
 708                    hi[node] = tip_index[node] + 1
 709                else:
 710                    los = [lo[c] for c in node._children]
 711                    his = [hi[c] for c in node._children]
 712                    lo[node] = min(los)
 713                    hi[node] = max(his)
 714            else:
 715                stack.append((node, True))
 716                for c in reversed(node._children):
 717                    stack.append((c, False))
 718
 719        tip_d = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.float64)
 720        for tip, idx in tip_index.items():
 721            tip_d[idx] = droot[tip]
 722
 723        mat = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=np.float64)
 724        for v in nodes:
 725            if v.is_leaf():
 726                continue
 727            dv = droot[v]
 728            ch = v._children
 729            m = len(ch)
 730            if m <= 12:
 731                # Low degree: broadcast the cross-clade block between each pair
 732                # of children (one write per pair's LCA).
 733                for s in range(m):
 734                    ls, hs = lo[ch[s]], hi[ch[s]]
 735                    ds = tip_d[ls:hs]
 736                    for t in range(s + 1, m):
 737                        lt, ht = lo[ch[t]], hi[ch[t]]
 738                        dt = tip_d[lt:ht]
 739                        cross = ds[:, None] + dt[None, :] - 2.0 * dv
 740                        mat[ls:hs, lt:ht] = cross
 741                        mat[lt:ht, ls:hs] = cross.T
 742            elif all(hi[c] - lo[c] == 1 for c in ch):
 743                # High degree but every child is a single tip (a star polytomy):
 744                # one contiguous full-block write; the diagonal is reset below.
 745                l, h = lo[v], hi[v]
 746                blk = tip_d[l:h]
 747                mat[l:h, l:h] = blk[:, None] + blk[None, :] - 2.0 * dv
 748            else:
 749                # High degree with sub-clades: one masked full-block shot that
 750                # keeps the within-clade cells already written by the children.
 751                l, h = lo[v], hi[v]
 752                blk = tip_d[l:h]
 753                full = blk[:, None] + blk[None, :] - 2.0 * dv
 754                cross = np.ones((h - l, h - l), dtype=bool)
 755                for c in ch:
 756                    cl, cht = lo[c], hi[c]
 757                    i0, j0 = cl - l, cht - l
 758                    cross[i0:j0, i0:j0] = False
 759                block = mat[l:h, l:h]
 760                block[cross] = full[cross]
 761
 762        np.fill_diagonal(mat, 0.0)
 763        return mat.tolist()
 764
 765    def get_depth_to_root(self, node: Tree) -> float:
 766        """Distance from ``node`` up to the root."""
 767        return self.get_distance(node, self)
 768
 769    def get_tree_length(self) -> float:
 770        """Sum of all branch lengths in the (sub)tree."""
 771        return sum(self._dist(n) for n in self if n.parent is not None)
 772
 773    def get_edge_lengths(self) -> list[float]:
 774        """Return the branch length of every non-root node (post-order)."""
 775        return [self._dist(n) for n in self if n.parent is not None]
 776
 777    @staticmethod
 778    def _dist(node: Tree) -> float:
 779        d = node.branch_length
 780        return 0.0 if d is None else float(d)
 781
 782    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 783    # data / annotation attachment
 784    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 785    def get_data(self, key: str, default=None):
 786        """Get an annotation value.
 787
 788        Annotations are looked up first (so a key that coincides with a method
 789        name, e.g. ``root``, still returns the stored annotation), then the
 790        genuine data slots (``name`` / ``branch_length`` / ``support``) and
 791        on-the-fly coordinate attributes.  Class attributes such as methods are
 792        never returned as data.
 793        """
 794        ann = self._annotations
 795        if ann is not None and key in ann:
 796            return ann[key]
 797        if key in ("name", "branch_length", "support"):
 798            return object.__getattribute__(self, key)
 799        if key.startswith("_"):
 800            # e.g. _x / _y set during layout, stored as annotations (never a method)
 801            return getattr(self, key, default)
 802        return default
 803
 804    def set_data(self, key: str, value) -> None:
 805        """Set an annotation value."""
 806        setattr(self, key, value)
 807
 808    def get_tipdata(self, key: str, default=None) -> dict[str, object]:
 809        """Return ``{tip_name: value}`` for a tip-level annotation."""
 810        return {n.name: n.get_data(key, default) for n in self.get_tips()}
 811
 812    def get_nodedata(self, key: str, default=None) -> dict[str, object]:
 813        """Return ``{node_name: value}`` for an internal-node annotation."""
 814        return {n.name: n.get_data(key, default) for n in self.get_internal_nodes()}
 815
 816    def set_nodedata(self, mapping: dict[str, object]) -> None:
 817        """Set a per-node annotation from ``{node_name: value}``."""
 818        for name, value in mapping.items():
 819            node = self.get_node_by_label(name)
 820            if node is not None:
 821                node.set_data(name, value)
 822
 823    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 824    # feature / data columns (toytree-style)
 825    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 826    @property
 827    def features(self) -> list[str]:
 828        """Sorted list of per-node data features (annotation columns)."""
 829        keys = set()
 830        for node in self.traverse("preorder"):
 831            ann = node._annotations
 832            if ann:
 833                keys.update(ann)
 834        return sorted(k for k in keys if not k.startswith("_"))
 835
 836    def set_feature(self, name: str, values) -> Tree:
 837        """Attach a per-node feature ``name``.
 838
 839        ``values`` may be a ``{node_label: value}`` dict, a list aligned to
 840        post-order nodes, or a scalar applied to every node.
 841        """
 842        if isinstance(values, dict):
 843            for label, value in values.items():
 844                node = self.get_node_by_label(str(label))
 845                if node is not None:
 846                    node.set_data(name, value)
 847        elif isinstance(values, (list, tuple)):
 848            for node, value in zip(self.traverse("postorder"), values):
 849                node.set_data(name, value)
 850        else:
 851            for node in self:
 852                node.set_data(name, values)
 853        return self
 854
 855    def get_feature(self, name: str, default=None) -> dict[str, object]:
 856        """Return ``{node_label: value}`` for a feature (post-order)."""
 857        return {n.name: n.get_data(name, default) for n in self}
 858
 859    def feature_map(self, *names: str) -> dict[str, list]:
 860        """Return ``{feature: [values aligned to post-order nodes]}``."""
 861        names = names or self.features
 862        nodes = list(self)
 863        return {name: [n.get_data(name) for n in nodes] for name in names}
 864
 865    def get_node_data(self, name: str, default=None) -> list:
 866        """Return the values of ``name`` aligned to post-order nodes."""
 867        return [n.get_data(name, default) for n in self]
 868
 869    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 870    # ergonomic access
 871    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 872    def __getitem__(self, i):
 873        """Convenient node access: name, index, slice, or list of names."""
 874        if isinstance(i, str):
 875            node = self.get_node_by_label(i)
 876            if node is None:
 877                raise KeyError(i)
 878            return node
 879        if isinstance(i, slice):
 880            return list(self.traverse("postorder"))[i]
 881        if isinstance(i, (list, tuple, set)):
 882            out = []
 883            for name in i:
 884                node = self.get_node_by_label(str(name))
 885                if node is None:
 886                    raise KeyError(name)
 887                out.append(node)
 888            return out
 889        nodes = list(self.traverse("postorder"))
 890        try:
 891            return nodes[i]
 892        except IndexError as e:
 893            raise IndexError(f"node index {i} out of range ({len(nodes)} nodes)") from e
 894
 895    def get_tip_labels(self) -> list[str]:
 896        """Alias of :attr:`tip_names` (list of tip labels)."""
 897        return self.get_tip_names()
 898
 899    def get_support_values(self) -> list[float]:
 900        """Support / bootstrap values of internal nodes (None dropped)."""
 901        return [n.support for n in self.get_internal_nodes() if n.support is not None]
 902
 903    def clades(self, *names) -> Tree | None:
 904        """Return the MRCA node of ``names`` (alias of :meth:`get_mrca`)."""
 905        return self.get_mrca(*names)
 906
 907    def get_tip_indices(self) -> dict[str, int]:
 908        """Return ``{tip_name: 0-based tip index}``."""
 909        return {t.name: i for i, t in enumerate(self.get_tips())}
 910
 911    def get_node_indices(self) -> dict[Tree, int]:
 912        """Return ``{node: 0-based post-order index}``."""
 913        return {n: i for i, n in enumerate(self)}
 914
 915    def get_index_map(self) -> dict[str, int]:
 916        """Return ``{node_label: post-order index}``."""
 917        return {n.name: i for i, n in enumerate(self)}
 918
 919    def write(self, *args, **kwargs) -> str | None:
 920        """Serialize this tree (see :func:`treeio.write`)."""
 921        from .io import write as _write
 922
 923        return _write(self, *args, **kwargs)
 924
 925    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 926    # topology manipulation
 927    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
 928    def ladderize(self, reverse: bool = False) -> Tree:
 929        """Reorder children so the tree is 'laddered' (sorted by clade size).
 930
 931        Mutates the tree in place and returns ``self``.
 932        """
 933        self._ladderize(reverse)
 934        return self
 935
 936    def _ladderize(self, reverse: bool) -> None:
 937        # bottom-up (post-order) re-sort using an explicit stack so a deeply
 938        # laddered tree does not overflow the recursion limit.
 939        stack = [(self, False)]
 940        while stack:
 941            node, visited = stack.pop()
 942            if visited:
 943                node.children = sorted(
 944                    node.children,
 945                    key=lambda c: (c.nleaves, c.name),
 946                    reverse=reverse,
 947                )
 948            else:
 949                stack.append((node, True))
 950                for ch in reversed(node._children):
 951                    stack.append((ch, False))
 952
 953    def rotate(self, node: Tree = None) -> Tree:
 954        """Rotate (reverse the order of) a node's children in place.
 955
 956        If ``node`` is ``None`` the root's children are rotated.  Returns self.
 957        """
 958        if node is None:
 959            node = self
 960        node.children = list(reversed(node.children))
 961        return self
 962
 963    def root(self, outgroup: Tree | str | Sequence = None) -> Tree:
 964        """Re-root the tree so ``outgroup`` is a basal (direct child) clade.
 965
 966        ``outgroup`` may be a :class:`Tree` node, a single tip name, or a
 967        sequence of names forming a clade.  The tree is modified in place and
 968        ``self`` remains the root.  Returns self.
 969        """
 970        if outgroup is None:
 971            return self
 972        out = self._resolve_clade(outgroup)
 973        if out is None:
 974            raise ValueError("outgroup not found in tree")
 975        if out is self:
 976            return self
 977
 978        # Re-root on the edge incident to ``out`` so it becomes a basal clade.
 979        # This is purely a root-placement change on the *fixed* unrooted topology:
 980        # every existing internal node and edge length is kept (the path between
 981        # ``out`` and the root is simply re-oriented), so tip-to-tip patristic
 982        # distances and the total tree length are unchanged.
 983        #
 984        # Build the chain of ancestors from ``out`` up to (but excluding) the
 985        # root: chain = [out, ..., child_of_root].  Every link is a direct
 986        # parent->child edge whose length is carried in ``branch_length``.
 987        chain = []
 988        node = out
 989        while node is not self:
 990            chain.append(node)
 991            node = node.parent
 992
 993        # ``out`` is already a direct child of the root: nothing to restructure,
 994        # just make it basal (first child).
 995        if len(chain) == 1:
 996            self._children.remove(out)
 997            self._children.insert(0, out)
 998            return self
 999
1000        out_node = chain[0]
1001        v1 = chain[1]  # out.parent, becomes the root of the sister clade
1002        vk = chain[-1]  # the child of the root on the path to ``out``
1003        old_b = [self._dist(x) for x in chain]
1004
1005        # The root's other subtrees (siblings of the path) are pulled down to
1006        # hang off ``vk``; each absorbs the former ``vk``->root edge length so
1007        # that the dissolved root edge is not lost.
1008        others = [c for c in self._children if c is not vk]
1009        old_others = {id(c): self._dist(c) for c in others}
1010
1011        # detach the outgroup and the siblings so the graph can be re-linked
1012        out_node._detach_from_parent()
1013        for c in others:
1014            c._detach_from_parent()
1015
1016        # ``v1`` becomes the direct child of the root; ``out`` keeps its edge so
1017        # the root is placed at ``v1``'s end of the (out, v1) edge.
1018        v1._detach_from_parent()
1019        v1._children = [c for c in v1._children if c is not out_node]
1020        v1.branch_length = 0.0
1021
1022        # Re-orient the inner path nodes: each chain[i+1] becomes a child of
1023        # chain[i] and inherits chain[i]'s former edge length.
1024        prev = v1
1025        for i in range(1, len(chain) - 1):
1026            vi = chain[i]
1027            vi1 = chain[i + 1]
1028            vi1._detach_from_parent()
1029            vi1._children = [c for c in vi1._children if c is not vi]
1030            vi1.branch_length = old_b[i]
1031            prev._children.append(vi1)
1032            vi1._parent = prev
1033            prev = vi1
1034
1035        # ``vk`` (now the deepest node of the re-oriented clade) absorbs the
1036        # root's former siblings.
1037        for c in others:
1038            add = old_b[-1]
1039            if c.branch_length is None:
1040                if add:
1041                    c.branch_length = float(add)
1042            else:
1043                c.branch_length = old_others[id(c)] + add
1044            prev._children.append(c)
1045            c._parent = prev
1046
1047        # final topology: root -> [out, v1] with out basal.
1048        self._children = [out_node, v1]
1049        out_node._parent = self
1050        v1._parent = self
1051        return self
1052
1053    def _resolve_clade(self, outgroup) -> Tree | None:
1054        """Resolve an outgroup spec into a node.
1055
1056        Accepts a :class:`Tree`, a tip/name string, or a sequence of names.
1057        """
1058        if isinstance(outgroup, Tree):
1059            return outgroup
1060        if isinstance(outgroup, str):
1061            return self.get_tip_by_label(outgroup) or self.get_node_by_label(outgroup)
1062        if isinstance(outgroup, (list, tuple, set)):
1063            return self.get_mrca(*list(outgroup))
1064        return None
1065
1066    def unroot(self) -> Tree:
1067        """Mark the tree as unrooted and collapse a degree-2 root.
1068
1069        A root with exactly two children is contracted so the root carries a
1070        degree-3-ish polytomy; the branch lengths on the two former root edges
1071        are averaged onto the surviving edges so the overall tree length is
1072        preserved.  The rooted state is recorded (``is_rooted()`` then reports
1073        ``False``).  Returns self.
1074        """
1075        self._is_rooted = False
1076        if len(self.children) == 2:
1077            c1, c2 = self.children
1078            new_dist = (self._dist(c1) + self._dist(c2)) / 2.0
1079            c1.branch_length = new_dist
1080            c2.branch_length = new_dist
1081        return self
1082
1083    def drop_tips(self, names: Iterable[str]) -> Tree:
1084        """Remove tips whose name is in ``names`` and prune emptied clades.
1085
1086        Mutates and returns ``self``.
1087        """
1088        banned = set(names)
1089        kept = [t for t in self.get_tips() if t.name not in banned]
1090        keptset = set(kept)
1091        if not keptset:
1092            self._children = []
1093            self.name = "unknown"
1094            self.branch_length = None
1095            return self
1096        self._prune_to(keptset)
1097        return self
1098
1099    def _prune_to(self, keptset: set) -> None:
1100        """Keep only descendants that lead to a tip in ``keptset``.
1101
1102        Generates a post-order plan on an explicit stack so a very deep
1103        caterpillar tree does not overflow the recursion limit.
1104        """
1105        stack = [(self, False)]
1106        while stack:
1107            node, visited = stack.pop()
1108            if visited:
1109                # children were already pruned + spliced (post-order), so only
1110                # the node itself needs collapsing here.
1111                node._splice_single_child()
1112            else:
1113                if node.is_leaf():
1114                    continue
1115                kept = [c for c in node._children if c._has_kept(keptset)]
1116                dropped = [c for c in node._children if not c._has_kept(keptset)]
1117                node._children = kept
1118                for c in dropped:
1119                    c._parent = None
1120                # schedule the node's own splice, then its (kept) children
1121                stack.append((node, True))
1122                for c in reversed(node._children):
1123                    c._parent = node
1124                    stack.append((c, False))
1125
1126    def _has_kept(self, keptset: set) -> bool:
1127        """True if any tip of this (sub)tree is in ``keptset``."""
1128        return any(t in keptset for t in self.get_tips())
1129
1130    def _splice_single_child(self) -> None:
1131        # Collapse any node (including the root) that has exactly one child by
1132        # promoting the child upward (its incoming branch length is added to the
1133        # child's, so total tree length is preserved).
1134        #
1135        # Only the node itself is collapsed here; ``_prune_to`` runs this in
1136        # post-order so each descendant is already collapsed before its parent,
1137        # and a collapse is a 1-for-1 child swap that never changes the parent's
1138        # child count.  This keeps the whole operation iterative (deep-tree safe)
1139        # while preserving identical behavior for normal trees.
1140        if len(self._children) == 1:
1141            child = self._children[0]
1142            if child.branch_length is not None or self.branch_length is not None:
1143                child.branch_length = (self._dist(self) + self._dist(child)) or None
1144            p = self._parent
1145            if p is not None:
1146                for i, c in enumerate(p._children):
1147                    if c is self:
1148                        p._children[i] = child
1149                        break
1150                child._parent = p
1151            else:
1152                # self is the root: adopt the child's identity and children
1153                self.name = child.name
1154                self.support = child.support
1155                for k, v in _iter_attrs(child):
1156                    setattr(self, k, v)
1157                self._children = list(child._children)
1158                for gc in self._children:
1159                    gc._parent = self
1160
1161    def prune(self, names: Iterable[str]) -> Tree:
1162        """Keep only the tips named in ``names``; everything else is dropped.
1163
1164        Mutates and returns ``self``.
1165        """
1166        return self.drop_tips(set(self.get_tip_names()) - set(names))
1167
1168    def collapse(self, node: Tree) -> Tree:
1169        """Collapse the clade under ``node`` into a single node.
1170
1171        ``node`` becomes a tip while keeping its name/support.  Returns self.
1172        """
1173        for c in node._children:
1174            c._parent = None
1175        node._children = []
1176        return self
1177
1178    def resolve_polytomies(self) -> Tree:
1179        """Insert (dummy, length-0) internal nodes to make the tree
1180        bifurcating.  Mutates and returns ``self``.
1181        """
1182        for c in self._children:
1183            c.resolve_polytomies()
1184        if len(self._children) > 2:
1185            kids = self._children
1186            first = kids[0]
1187            tail = kids[1]
1188            for k in kids[2:]:
1189                dummy = Tree("internal", branch_length=0.0)
1190                dummy._parent = self
1191                dummy._children = [tail, k]
1192                tail._parent = dummy
1193                k._parent = dummy
1194                tail = dummy
1195            self._children = [first, tail]
1196            first._parent = self
1197            tail._parent = self
1198        return self
1199
1200    def get_dummy_polytomy(self) -> Tree:
1201        """Return a copy of the tree's root polytomy resolved to a dummy node."""
1202        copy = self.copy()
1203        root = copy
1204        if len(root._children) > 2:
1205            kids = root._children
1206            dummy = Tree("internal", branch_length=0.0)
1207            dummy._children = list(kids)
1208            for k in kids:
1209                k._parent = dummy
1210            root._children = [dummy]
1211            dummy._parent = root
1212        return copy
1213
1214    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
1215    # copy / export
1216    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
1217    def copy(self, deep: bool = True) -> Tree:
1218        """Independent deep copy of the subtree rooted at self."""
1219        new = Tree()
1220        # iterative clone (copes with very deep trees without recursion)
1221        new.name = self.name
1222        new.branch_length = self.branch_length
1223        new.support = self.support
1224        _copy_attrs(self, new)
1225        stack = [(self, new)]
1226        while stack:
1227            src, dst = stack.pop()
1228            for child in src.children:
1229                nc = Tree()
1230                nc.name = child.name
1231                nc.branch_length = child.branch_length
1232                nc.support = child.support
1233                _copy_attrs(child, nc)
1234                nc._parent = dst
1235                dst._children.append(nc)
1236                stack.append((child, nc))
1237        return new
1238
1239    def clone(self) -> Tree:
1240        """Alias of :meth:`copy`."""
1241        return self.copy()
1242
1243    def get_subtree(self, node: Tree) -> Tree:
1244        """Return a copy of the clade rooted at ``node``."""
1245        return node.copy()
1246
1247    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
1248    # coordinates for plotting
1249    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
1250    def get_y_and_x(self, x_as_branch: bool = True, root_dist: float = 0.0):
1251        """Assign ``x`` / ``y`` coordinates for a rectangular layout.
1252
1253        ``x`` is the cumulative branch length from the root (or the node
1254        index if ``x_as_branch`` is False); ``y`` is the tip index position
1255        (internal nodes get the midpoint of their children).  Mutates the
1256        nodes in place.  Returns ``self`` so it can be used fluently.
1257        """
1258        self._assign_layout(x_as_branch, root_dist)
1259        return self
1260
1261    def _assign_layout(self, x_as_branch, root_dist) -> None:
1262        leaves = self.get_tips()
1263        for i, leaf in enumerate(leaves):
1264            leaf._y = i
1265
1266        if x_as_branch:
1267            # accumulate branch length from the root downward (iterative)
1268            stack = [(self, root_dist)]
1269            while stack:
1270                node, x = stack.pop()
1271                node._x = x
1272                for c in node.children:
1273                    stack.append((c, x + self._dist(c)))
1274        else:
1275            # x is simply the post-order node index
1276            for i, node in enumerate(self.traverse("postorder")):
1277                node._x = float(i)
1278
1279        # y for internal nodes is the midpoint of their children.  Iterate in
1280        # post-order (children first) so each child's _y is already computed.
1281        for node in self.get_internal_nodes():
1282            node._y = (node.children[0]._y + node.children[-1]._y) / 2.0
1283        return self
1284

1286    # misc
1287    # ---------------------------------------------------------------- ---
1288    def get_node2index(self) -> dict[Tree, int]:
1289        """Map every node to a 0-based index in post-order."""
1290        return {n: i for i, n in enumerate(self)}
1291
1292    def get_index2node(self) -> list[Tree]:
1293        return list(self)
1294
1295    def edge_vector(self) -> list[tuple]:
1296        """Return list of ``(parent_index, child_index)`` in post-order."""
1297        idx = self.get_node2index()
1298        return [(idx[n._parent], idx[n]) for n in self if n._parent is not None]

1344        """Build a Tree from an alignment via distance + neighbour joining.
1345
1346        ``sequences`` may be a ``{name: sequence}`` dict, iterable of
1347        ``(name, sequence)`` pairs, raw sequence strings, or Biopython
1348        ``SeqRecord`` objects (aligned, equal length).  ``model`` selects the
1349        distance model (``"p"`` or ``"jc"`` / ``"jc69"``).

1357    def as_dict(self, **fields) -> dict:
1358        """Serialize to a nested python dict (deep-tree safe, iterative).
1359
1360        By default ``name``, ``branch_length`` and ``support`` are emitted for
1361        every node, and ``children`` follows the subtree.  Custom annotation
1362        fields can be requested via keyword ``name->attr``, e.g.
1363        ``as_dict(rate="rate")``.
1364        """
1365        field_map = {
1366            "name": "name",
1367            "branch_length": "branch_length",
1368            "support": "support",
1369        }
1370        field_map.update(fields)
1371
1372        def make(node):
1373            return {key: node.get_data(attr) for key, attr in field_map.items()}
1374
1375        root = make(self)
1376        # iterative post-order assembly (no recursion)
1377        out = {id(self): root}
1378        stack = [(self, root)]
1379        while stack:
1380            node, dic = stack.pop()
1381            if not node._children:
1382                continue
1383            kids = []
1384            for c in node._children:
1385                cd = make(c)
1386                kids.append(cd)
1387                out[id(c)] = cd
1388                stack.append((c, cd))
1389            dic["children"] = kids
1390        return root

74    def __init__(self, name="unknown", branch_length=None, support=None, **kwargs):
75        """Create a node.
76
77        Each argument is stored as an attribute on the node.  ``branch_length``
78        is the branch length leading to this node (``None`` if unknown) and
79        ``support`` the support / bootstrap value (``None`` if unknown).
80
81        Keyword arguments become arbitrary per-node annotations (stored in a
82        single dict).  If ``parent`` is supplied the node is attached
83        underneath it.
84        """
85        object.__setattr__(self, "name", name)
86        object.__setattr__(self, "branch_length", branch_length)
87        object.__setattr__(self, "support", support)
88        object.__setattr__(self, "_parent", None)
89        object.__setattr__(self, "_children", [])
90        object.__setattr__(self, "_annotations", None)
91
92        # support any value, attached as annotation.
93        for key, value in kwargs.items():
94            if key == "parent":
95                self.parent = value
96            else:
97                setattr(self, key, value)

def is_binary(self) -> bool: 
285    def is_binary(self) -> bool:
286        """Check the (sub)tree is fully bifurcating (no multifurcation).
287
288        Implemented iteratively (explicit stack) so it copes with very deep
289        trees without hitting the recursion limit.
290        """
291        stack = [self]
292        while stack:
293            node = stack.pop()
294            if node.is_leaf():
295                continue
296            if len(node._children) != 2:
297                return False
298            stack.extend(node._children)
299        return True

def is_monophyletic(self, *names) -> bool: 
378    def is_monophyletic(self, *names) -> bool:
379        """Return ``True`` if *all* ``names`` form a single clade."""
380        tips = {n.name for n in self.get_tips()}
381        target = set(names)
382        if not target <= tips:
383            return False
384        # find node containing exactly target
385        for node in self.get_nodes():
386            below = {n.name for n in node.get_tips()}
387            if below == target:
388                return True
389        return False

Return True if all names form a single clade.

def is_outgroup(self, *names) -> bool: 
391    def is_outgroup(self, *names) -> bool:
392        """True when the clade of ``names`` is sibling to everything else."""
393        tips = {n.name for n in self.get_tips()}
394        target = set(names)
395        if not target <= tips:
396            return False
397        # an outgroup splits the root into exactly two children
398        if len(self.children) != 2:
399            return False
400        for c in self.children:
401            if {n.name for n in c.get_tips()} == target:
402                return True
403        return False

def traverse(self, order: str = 'preorder') -> Iterator[Tree]: 
408    def traverse(self, order: str = "preorder") -> Iterator[Tree]:
409        """Iterate over descendant nodes.
410
411        order: one of ``'preorder'``, ``'postorder'``, ``'levelorder'``.
412        The node ``self`` is included.  (Iterative, so it copes with very
413        deep trees without hitting the recursion limit.)
414        """
415        if order == "postorder":
416            stack = [(self, False)]
417            while stack:
418                node, visited = stack.pop()
419                if visited:
420                    yield node
421                else:
422                    stack.append((node, True))
423                    for ch in reversed(node._children):
424                        stack.append((ch, False))
425        elif order == "levelorder":
426            frontier = [self]
427            while frontier:
428                nxt = []
429                for node in frontier:
430                    yield node
431                    nxt.extend(node._children)
432                frontier = nxt
433        elif order == "preorder":
434            stack = [self]
435            while stack:
436                node = stack.pop()
437                yield node
438                # push children in reverse so they are visited left-to-right
439                for ch in reversed(node._children):
440                    stack.append(ch)
441        else:
442            raise ValueError(f"unknown order {order!r}")

Iterate over descendant nodes.

448            if cur is self:

451        return False

463        Use this for bulk label lookups (e.g. data attachment) instead of

470                index[name] = node

def get_mrca(self, *nodes) -> Tree | None: 
521    def get_mrca(self, *nodes) -> Tree | None:
522        """Return the most recent common ancestor of a set of nodes.
523
524        Accepts ``Tree`` nodes or names (strings).
525        """
526        resolved = [
527            n if isinstance(n, Tree) else self.get_node_by_label(n) for n in nodes
528        ]
529        if not resolved or any(n is None for n in resolved):
530            return None
531        out = resolved[0]
532        for n in resolved[1:]:
533            out = self.get_common_ancestor(out, n)
534        return out

def get_distance(self, node1: Tree, node2: Tree) -> float: 
598    def get_distance(self, node1: Tree, node2: Tree) -> float:
599        """Return the patristic distance between two nodes.
600
601        Branch lengths are summed along the path; missing (``None``) branch
602        lengths are treated as 0.
603        """
604        if not isinstance(node1, Tree) or not isinstance(node2, Tree):
605            raise TypeError("get_distance expects Tree nodes")
606
607        lca = self._lca_node(node1, node2)
608        if lca is None:
609            raise ValueError("nodes are not in the same tree")
610
611        d = 0.0
612        cur = node1
613        while cur is not lca:
614            bl = cur.branch_length
615            d += 0.0 if bl is None else float(bl)
616            cur = cur._parent
617        cur = node2
618        while cur is not lca:
619            bl = cur.branch_length
620            d += 0.0 if bl is None else float(bl)
621            cur = cur._parent
622        return d

Return the patristic distance between two nodes.

Branch lengths are summed along the path; missing (None) branch lengths are treated as 0.

def get_cophenetic_distance(self) -> list[list[float]]: 
624    def get_cophenetic_distance(self) -> list[list[float]]:
625        """Return the pairwise patristic distance matrix for all tips.
626
627        Uses ``dist(a, b) = D(a) + D(b) - 2*D(mrca(a, b))`` where ``D(x)`` is
628        the *branch-length* distance from the root down to ``x``.  ``D`` is
629        computed once in a single traversal, then the ``n x n`` matrix is filled
630        with numpy so the pairwise loop runs in C instead of Python (no per-pair
631        Python LCA walk).  Every tip pair is written exactly once -- at its most
632        recent common ancestor -- by filling the cross-clade block between each
633        pair of children of that node; deeper clades already hold their own
634        within-clade values.  This is ``O(n^2)`` element work for any shape.
635        Iterative (explicit stacks), so it copes with very deep trees without
636        hitting the recursion limit.
637        """
638        import math
639
640        tips = self.get_tips()
641        n = len(tips)
642        if n < 2:
643            return [[0.0] * n for _ in range(n)]
644
645        import numpy as np
646
647        # Pre-order sweep: assign tip indices (contiguous per clade) and the
648        # branch-length distance D from the root down to every node.
649        nodes = []
650        droot = {}
651        tip_index = {}
652        tip_counter = 0
653        finite = True
654        max_bl = 0.0
655        min_pos_bl = None
656        stack = [(self, 0.0)]
657        while stack:
658            node, parent_d = stack.pop()
659            bl = node.branch_length
660            if bl is not None:
661                fb = abs(float(bl))
662                max_bl = max(max_bl, fb)
663                if fb and (min_pos_bl is None or fb < min_pos_bl):
664                    min_pos_bl = fb
665            d = parent_d + (0.0 if bl is None else float(bl))
666            if finite and not math.isfinite(d):
667                finite = False
668            droot[node] = d
669            nodes.append(node)
670            if node.is_leaf():
671                tip_index[node] = tip_counter
672                tip_counter += 1
673            for c in reversed(node._children):
674                stack.append((c, d))
675
676        # ``inf`` / ``nan`` branch lengths break the ``D(a)+D(b)-2*D(lca)``
677        # identity (``inf - inf`` is ``nan``), so fall back to the exact
678        # per-pair path sum for such (pathological) trees.  ``get_distance``
679        # reproduces the original LCA + summation result bit for bit.
680        #
681        # The same identity also suffers catastrophic cancellation when branch
682        # lengths span a huge dynamic range (e.g. a 1e15 edge next to a 1e-3
683        # tip edge): the tip values are lost in ``D`` and the result collapses
684        # to 0 even though ``get_distance`` is correct.  Treat that as the same
685        # non-finite/ill-conditioned case so the exact per-pair path sum is
686        # used instead.
687        if max_bl and min_pos_bl and min_pos_bl < max_bl * 2.0**-40:
688            finite = False
689        if not finite:
690            mat = [[0.0] * n for _ in range(n)]
691            for i in range(n):
692                a = tips[i]
693                for j in range(i + 1, n):
694                    d = self.get_distance(a, tips[j])
695                    mat[i][j] = mat[j][i] = d
696            return mat
697
698        # Post-order pass records the contiguous tip-index range [lo, hi) that
699        # each node's clade occupies (used as the numpy block to fill).
700        lo = {}
701        hi = {}
702        stack = [(self, False)]
703        while stack:
704            node, visited = stack.pop()
705            if visited:
706                if node.is_leaf():
707                    lo[node] = tip_index[node]
708                    hi[node] = tip_index[node] + 1
709                else:
710                    los = [lo[c] for c in node._children]
711                    his = [hi[c] for c in node._children]
712                    lo[node] = min(los)
713                    hi[node] = max(his)
714            else:
715                stack.append((node, True))
716                for c in reversed(node._children):
717                    stack.append((c, False))
718
719        tip_d = np.zeros(n, dtype=np.float64)
720        for tip, idx in tip_index.items():
721            tip_d[idx] = droot[tip]
722
723        mat = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=np.float64)
724        for v in nodes:
725            if v.is_leaf():
726                continue
727            dv = droot[v]
728            ch = v._children
729            m = len(ch)
730            if m <= 12:
731                # Low degree: broadcast the cross-clade block between each pair
732                # of children (one write per pair's LCA).
733                for s in range(m):
734                    ls, hs = lo[ch[s]], hi[ch[s]]
735                    ds = tip_d[ls:hs]
736                    for t in range(s + 1, m):
737                        lt, ht = lo[ch[t]], hi[ch[t]]
738                        dt = tip_d[lt:ht]
739                        cross = ds[:, None] + dt[None, :] - 2.0 * dv
740                        mat[ls:hs, lt:ht] = cross
741                        mat[lt:ht, ls:hs] = cross.T
742            elif all(hi[c] - lo[c] == 1 for c in ch):
743                # High degree but every child is a single tip (a star polytomy):
744                # one contiguous full-block write; the diagonal is reset below.
745                l, h = lo[v], hi[v]
746                blk = tip_d[l:h]
747                mat[l:h, l:h] = blk[:, None] + blk[None, :] - 2.0 * dv
748            else:
749                # High degree with sub-clades: one masked full-block shot that
750                # keeps the within-clade cells already written by the children.
751                l, h = lo[v], hi[v]
752                blk = tip_d[l:h]
753                full = blk[:, None] + blk[None, :] - 2.0 * dv
754                cross = np.ones((h - l, h - l), dtype=bool)
755                for c in ch:
756                    cl, cht = lo[c], hi[c]
757                    i0, j0 = cl - l, cht - l
758                    cross[i0:j0, i0:j0] = False
759                block = mat[l:h, l:h]
760                block[cross] = full[cross]
761
762        np.fill_diagonal(mat, 0.0)
763        return mat.tolist()

Return the pairwise patristic distance matrix for all tips.

Uses dist(a, b) = D(a) + D(b) - 2*D(mrca(a, b)) where D(x) is the branch-length distance from the root down to x. D is computed once in a single traversal, then the n x n matrix is filled with numpy so the pairwise loop runs in C instead of Python (no per-pair Python LCA walk). Every tip pair is written exactly once -- at its most recent common ancestor -- by filling the cross-clade block between each pair of children of that node; deeper clades already hold their own within-clade values. This is O(n^2) element work for any shape. Iterative (explicit stacks), so it copes with very deep trees without hitting the recursion limit.

785    def get_data(self, key: str, default=None):
786        """Get an annotation value.
787
788        Annotations are looked up first (so a key that coincides with a method
789        name, e.g. ``root``, still returns the stored annotation), then the
790        genuine data slots (``name`` / ``branch_length`` / ``support``) and
791        on-the-fly coordinate attributes.  Class attributes such as methods are
792        never returned as data.

798            return object.__getattribute__(self, key)
799        if key.startswith("_"):
800            # e.g. _x / _y set during layout, stored as annotations (never a method)
801            return getattr(self, key, default)
802        return default

def root( self, outgroup: Tree | str | Sequence = None) -> Tree: 
 963    def root(self, outgroup: Tree | str | Sequence = None) -> Tree:
 964        """Re-root the tree so ``outgroup`` is a basal (direct child) clade.
 965
 966        ``outgroup`` may be a :class:`Tree` node, a single tip name, or a
 967        sequence of names forming a clade.  The tree is modified in place and
 968        ``self`` remains the root.  Returns self.
 969        """
 970        if outgroup is None:
 971            return self
 972        out = self._resolve_clade(outgroup)
 973        if out is None:
 974            raise ValueError("outgroup not found in tree")
 975        if out is self:
 976            return self
 977
 978        # Re-root on the edge incident to ``out`` so it becomes a basal clade.
 979        # This is purely a root-placement change on the *fixed* unrooted topology:
 980        # every existing internal node and edge length is kept (the path between
 981        # ``out`` and the root is simply re-oriented), so tip-to-tip patristic
 982        # distances and the total tree length are unchanged.
 983        #
 984        # Build the chain of ancestors from ``out`` up to (but excluding) the
 985        # root: chain = [out, ..., child_of_root].  Every link is a direct
 986        # parent->child edge whose length is carried in ``branch_length``.
 987        chain = []
 988        node = out
 989        while node is not self:
 990            chain.append(node)
 991            node = node.parent
 992
 993        # ``out`` is already a direct child of the root: nothing to restructure,
 994        # just make it basal (first child).
 995        if len(chain) == 1:
 996            self._children.remove(out)
 997            self._children.insert(0, out)
 998            return self
 999
1000        out_node = chain[0]
1001        v1 = chain[1]  # out.parent, becomes the root of the sister clade
1002        vk = chain[-1]  # the child of the root on the path to ``out``
1003        old_b = [self._dist(x) for x in chain]
1004
1005        # The root's other subtrees (siblings of the path) are pulled down to
1006        # hang off ``vk``; each absorbs the former ``vk``->root edge length so
1007        # that the dissolved root edge is not lost.
1008        others = [c for c in self._children if c is not vk]
1009        old_others = {id(c): self._dist(c) for c in others}
1010
1011        # detach the outgroup and the siblings so the graph can be re-linked
1012        out_node._detach_from_parent()
1013        for c in others:
1014            c._detach_from_parent()
1015
1016        # ``v1`` becomes the direct child of the root; ``out`` keeps its edge so
1017        # the root is placed at ``v1``'s end of the (out, v1) edge.
1018        v1._detach_from_parent()
1019        v1._children = [c for c in v1._children if c is not out_node]
1020        v1.branch_length = 0.0
1021
1022        # Re-orient the inner path nodes: each chain[i+1] becomes a child of
1023        # chain[i] and inherits chain[i]'s former edge length.
1024        prev = v1
1025        for i in range(1, len(chain) - 1):
1026            vi = chain[i]
1027            vi1 = chain[i + 1]
1028            vi1._detach_from_parent()
1029            vi1._children = [c for c in vi1._children if c is not vi]
1030            vi1.branch_length = old_b[i]
1031            prev._children.append(vi1)
1032            vi1._parent = prev
1033            prev = vi1
1034
1035        # ``vk`` (now the deepest node of the re-oriented clade) absorbs the
1036        # root's former siblings.
1037        for c in others:
1038            add = old_b[-1]
1039            if c.branch_length is None:
1040                if add:
1041                    c.branch_length = float(add)
1042            else:
1043                c.branch_length = old_others[id(c)] + add
1044            prev._children.append(c)
1045            c._parent = prev
1046
1047        # final topology: root -> [out, v1] with out basal.
1048        self._children = [out_node, v1]
1049        out_node._parent = self
1050        v1._parent = self
1051        return self

Re-root the tree so outgroup is a basal (direct child) clade.

outgroup may be a Tree node, a single tip name, or a sequence of names forming a clade. The tree is modified in place and self remains the root. Returns self.

def unroot(self) -> Tree: 
1066    def unroot(self) -> Tree:
1067        """Mark the tree as unrooted and collapse a degree-2 root.
1068
1069        A root with exactly two children is contracted so the root carries a
1070        degree-3-ish polytomy; the branch lengths on the two former root edges
1071        are averaged onto the surviving edges so the overall tree length is
1072        preserved.  The rooted state is recorded (``is_rooted()`` then reports
1073        ``False``).  Returns self.
1074        """
1075        self._is_rooted = False
1076        if len(self.children) == 2:
1077            c1, c2 = self.children
1078            new_dist = (self._dist(c1) + self._dist(c2)) / 2.0
1079            c1.branch_length = new_dist
1080            c2.branch_length = new_dist
1081        return self

Mark the tree as unrooted and collapse a degree-2 root.

A root with exactly two children is contracted so the root carries a degree-3-ish polytomy; the branch lengths on the two former root edges are averaged onto the surviving edges so the overall tree length is preserved. The rooted state is recorded (is_rooted() then reports False). Returns self.

def drop_tips(self, names: Iterable[str]) -> Tree: 
1083    def drop_tips(self, names: Iterable[str]) -> Tree:
1084        """Remove tips whose name is in ``names`` and prune emptied clades.
1085
1086        Mutates and returns ``self``.
1087        """
1088        banned = set(names)
1089        kept = [t for t in self.get_tips() if t.name not in banned]
1090        keptset = set(kept)
1091        if not keptset:
1092            self._children = []
1093            self.name = "unknown"
1094            self.branch_length = None
1095            return self
1096        self._prune_to(keptset)
1097        return self

Remove tips whose name is in names and prune emptied clades.

Mutates and returns self.

def prune(self, names: Iterable[str]) -> Tree: 
1161    def prune(self, names: Iterable[str]) -> Tree:
1162        """Keep only the tips named in ``names``; everything else is dropped.
1163
1164        Mutates and returns ``self``.
1165        """
1166        return self.drop_tips(set(self.get_tip_names()) - set(names))

def collapse(self, node: Tree) -> Tree: 
1168    def collapse(self, node: Tree) -> Tree:
1169        """Collapse the clade under ``node`` into a single node.
1170
1171        ``node`` becomes a tip while keeping its name/support.  Returns self.
1172        """
1173        for c in node._children:
1174            c._parent = None
1175        node._children = []
1176        return self

node becomes a tip while keeping its name/support. Returns self.

def resolve_polytomies(self) -> Tree: 
1178    def resolve_polytomies(self) -> Tree:
1179        """Insert (dummy, length-0) internal nodes to make the tree
1180        bifurcating.  Mutates and returns ``self``.
1181        """
1182        for c in self._children:
1183            c.resolve_polytomies()
1184        if len(self._children) > 2:
1185            kids = self._children
1186            first = kids[0]
1187            tail = kids[1]
1188            for k in kids[2:]:
1189                dummy = Tree("internal", branch_length=0.0)
1190                dummy._parent = self
1191                dummy._children = [tail, k]
1192                tail._parent = dummy
1193                k._parent = dummy
1194                tail = dummy
1195            self._children = [first, tail]
1196            first._parent = self
1197            tail._parent = self
1198        return self

Insert (dummy, length-0) internal nodes to make the tree bifurcating. Mutates and returns self.

def get_dummy_polytomy(self) -> Tree: 
1200    def get_dummy_polytomy(self) -> Tree:
1201        """Return a copy of the tree's root polytomy resolved to a dummy node."""
1202        copy = self.copy()
1203        root = copy
1204        if len(root._children) > 2:
1205            kids = root._children
1206            dummy = Tree("internal", branch_length=0.0)
1207            dummy._children = list(kids)
1208            for k in kids:
1209                k._parent = dummy
1210            root._children = [dummy]
1211            dummy._parent = root
1212        return copy

Return a copy of the tree's root polytomy resolved to a dummy node.

def copy(self, deep: bool = True) -> Tree: 
1217    def copy(self, deep: bool = True) -> Tree:
1218        """Independent deep copy of the subtree rooted at self."""
1219        new = Tree()
1220        # iterative clone (copes with very deep trees without recursion)
1221        new.name = self.name
1222        new.branch_length = self.branch_length
1223        new.support = self.support
1224        _copy_attrs(self, new)
1225        stack = [(self, new)]
1226        while stack:
1227            src, dst = stack.pop()
1228            for child in src.children:
1229                nc = Tree()
1230                nc.name = child.name
1231                nc.branch_length = child.branch_length
1232                nc.support = child.support
1233                _copy_attrs(child, nc)
1234                nc._parent = dst
1235                dst._children.append(nc)
1236                stack.append((child, nc))
1237        return new

Independent deep copy of the subtree rooted at self.

def as_dict(self, **fields) -> dict: 
1357    def as_dict(self, **fields) -> dict:
1358        """Serialize to a nested python dict (deep-tree safe, iterative).
1359
1360        By default ``name``, ``branch_length`` and ``support`` are emitted for
1361        every node, and ``children`` follows the subtree.  Custom annotation
1362        fields can be requested via keyword ``name->attr``, e.g.
1363        ``as_dict(rate="rate")``.
1364        """
1365        field_map = {
1366            "name": "name",
1367            "branch_length": "branch_length",
1368            "support": "support",
1369        }
1370        field_map.update(fields)
1371
1372        def make(node):
1373            return {key: node.get_data(attr) for key, attr in field_map.items()}
1374
1375        root = make(self)
1376        # iterative post-order assembly (no recursion)
1377        out = {id(self): root}
1378        stack = [(self, root)]
1379        while stack:
1380            node, dic = stack.pop()
1381            if not node._children:
1382                continue
1383            kids = []
1384            for c in node._children:
1385                cd = make(c)
1386                kids.append(cd)
1387                out[id(c)] = cd
1388                stack.append((c, cd))
1389            dic["children"] = kids
1390        return root

Serialize to a nested python dict (deep-tree safe, iterative).

By default name, branch_length and support are emitted for every node, and children follows the subtree. Custom annotation fields can be requested via keyword name->attr, e.g. as_dict(rate="rate").

1492    """An OO, matplotlib-compatible tree plotter.
1493
1494    Holds a real :class:`matplotlib.axes.Axes` and exposes marker methods that
1495    delegate to the matching ``ax`` method (``.plot_edges()``,
1496    ``.scatter_tips()``, ``.scatter_nodes()``, ``.plot_tip_labels()``,
1497    ``.plot_node_labels()``, ``.legend()``, ``.savefig()``)."""

1499    def __init__(
1500        self,
1501        tree: Tree,
1502        ax=None,
1503        layout: str = "rectangular",
1504        edge_color: str = "#333333",
1505        edge_width: float = 1.2,
1506        **kw,
1507    ):
1508        self.tree = tree
1509        self.layout = layout
1510        self.edge_color = edge_color
1511        self.edge_width = edge_width
1512        self.reverse_x = kw.pop("reverse_x", False)
1513        self.coords = tree_coords(tree, layout=layout, reverse_x=self.reverse_x)
1514        self._ax = _new_axes(tree, layout, self.reverse_x, ax=ax, **kw)
1515

1522        self,
1523        size: float = 18,
1524        color=None,
1525        aes: str | None = None,
1526        cmap: str = "viridis",
1527        **kw,
1528    ):
1529        """Mark tips (``ax.scatter``).  ``aes`` colours by a per-tip field."""
1530        tips = self.tree.get_tips()
1531        c, _, _ = _tip_colors_for(self.tree, tips, None, aes, cmap, self.edge_color)
1532        return self._ax.scatter(
1533            [self.coords[t][0] for t in tips],
