1551    def plot_tip_labels(
1552        self,
1553        size: int = 10,
1554        aes: str | None = None,
1555        color=None,
1556        radial_offset: float = 0.04,
1557        **kw,
1558    ):
1559        """Write tip labels; radial layouts rotate them (collision avoidance).
1560
1561        ``aes`` colours the labels by a per-tip field."""
1562        polar = self.layout in _POLAR_LAYOUTS
1563        c, _, _ = _tip_colors_for(
1564            self.tree, self.tree.get_tips(), None, aes, "viridis", self.edge_color
1565        )
1566        out = []
1567        for i, tip in enumerate(self.tree.get_tips()):
1568            x, y = self.coords[tip]
1569            col = color or (c[i] if isinstance(c[i], str) else self.edge_color)
1570            out.append(
1571                _write_tip_label(
1572                    self._ax, x, y, tip.name, polar, col, size, offset=radial_offset
1573                )
1574            )
1575        return out
1576
1577    def plot_node_labels(self, size: int = 8, color="#666666", show_support=True, **kw):
1578        """Write internal-node labels / support values (``ax.text``)."""
1579        out = []
1580        for node in self.tree.get_internal_nodes():
1581            label = node.name
1582            if (
1583                (label in (None, "", "unknown"))
1584                and show_support
1585                and node.support is not None
1586            ):
1587                label = str(node.support)
1588            if label in (None, "", "unknown"):
1589                continue
1590            x, y = self.coords[node]
1591            out.append(
1592                self._ax.text(
1593                    x,
1594                    y,
1595                    label,
1596                    fontsize=size,
1597                    color=color,
1598                    ha="center",

1600                    **kw,
1601                )

1605    def plot_edges(
1606        self,
1607        aes: str | None = None,
1608        color=None,
1609        width=None,
1610        cmap: str = "viridis",
1611        norm=None,
1612    ):
1613        """Draw the branches.
1614
1615        If ``aes`` names a per-node field, each edge is coloured by the child
1616        node's value (a continuous colour scale); call :meth:`add_colorbar` to
1617        add a colourbar.  Otherwise a single ``LineCollection`` is used.
1618        """
1619        from matplotlib.collections import LineCollection
1620
1621        segments = edge_segments(self.tree, self.coords, self.layout)
1622        if aes is not None:
1623            import matplotlib
1624            import numpy as np
1625
1626            vals = [
1627                c.get_data(aes)
1628                for c in self.tree.traverse("preorder")
1629                if c.parent is not None
1630            ]
1631            arr = np.asarray(
1632                [np.nan if v is None else float(v) for v in vals], dtype=float
1633            )
1634            lo = float(np.nanmin(arr))
1635            hi = float(np.nanmax(arr))
1636            if not np.isfinite(lo) or lo == hi:
1637                lo, hi = 0.0, 1.0
1638            if norm is None:
1639                norm = matplotlib.colors.Normalize(vmin=lo, vmax=hi)
1640            cmap_obj = matplotlib.colormaps.get_cmap(cmap)
1641            lc = LineCollection(
1642                segments,
1643                array=arr,
1644                cmap=cmap_obj,
1645                norm=norm,
1646                linewidths=width or self.edge_width,
1647                capstyle="round",
1648            )
1649            self._edge_mappable = lc
1650        else:
1651            self._edge_mappable = None
1652            lc = LineCollection(
1653                segments,
1654                colors=color or self.edge_color,
1655                linewidths=width or self.edge_width,
1656                capstyle="round",
1657            )
1658        self._ax.add_collection(lc)
1659        self._ax.autoscale()
1660        return lc
1661
1662    def add_colorbar(self, label: str = "value", **kwargs):
1663        """Add a continuous colourbar for the ``aes``-coloured branches."""
1664        if getattr(self, "_edge_mappable", None) is None:
1665            raise RuntimeError("plot_edges(aes=...) must be called first")
1666        cb = self._ax.figure.colorbar(self._edge_mappable, ax=self._ax, **kwargs)
1667        if label:
1668            cb.set_label(label)
1669        return cb
1670
1671    def legend_for(self, field: str, cmap: str = "viridis"):
1672        """Add a continuous colourbar or categorical legend for ``field``.
1673
1674        Uses the tip values of ``field``; numeric -> colourbar, categorical -> a
1675        legend of categories.
1676        """
1677        import matplotlib
1678
1679        tips = self.tree.get_tips()
1680        values = {t.name: t.get_data(field) for t in tips}
1681        known = {k: v for k, v in values.items() if v is not None}
1682        if known and all(isinstance(v, (int, float)) for v in known.values()):
1683            import numpy as np
1684
1685            arr = np.array(
1686                [
1687                    float(values[t.name]) if values[t.name] is not None else np.nan
1688                    for t in tips
1689                ]
1690            )
1691            lo = float(np.nanmin(arr))
1692            hi = float(np.nanmax(arr))
1693            if not np.isfinite(lo) or lo == hi:
1694                lo, hi = 0.0, 1.0
1695            norm = matplotlib.colors.Normalize(vmin=lo, vmax=hi)
1696            mappable = matplotlib.cm.ScalarMappable(
1697                norm=norm, cmap=matplotlib.colormaps.get_cmap(cmap)
1698            )
1699            cb = self._ax.figure.colorbar(mappable, ax=self._ax)
1700            cb.set_label(field, fontsize=9)
1701            return cb
1702        cats = sorted(set(known.values()), key=str)
1703        pal = named_palette([str(c) for c in cats])
1704        import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
1705
1706        handles = [mpatches.Patch(color=pal[str(c)], label=str(c)) for c in cats]
1707        return self._ax.legend(
1708            handles=handles,
1709            title=field,
1710            fontsize=8,
1711            title_fontsize=9,
1712            loc="upper left",
1713            bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1.0),
1714        )
1715
1716    def theme(self, style: str = "clean", **kwargs):
1717        """Apply a :func:`tree_theme` style to the axes."""
1718        tree_theme(self._ax, style=style, **kwargs)
1719        return self
1720
1721    def scale_bar(
1722        self,

1730

1733
1734    def savefig(self, path, **kwargs):

def add_ring( tree, field, ax=None, layout='circular', cmap='viridis', discrete=False, ring_width=0.06, start=0.12, pad=0.02, colorbar=False, colorbar_label=None, palette=None, norm=None, zorder=1.0, coords=None, **kwargs): 
1188def add_ring(
1189    tree,
1190    field,
1191    ax=None,
1192    layout="circular",
1193    cmap="viridis",
1194    discrete=False,
1195    ring_width=0.06,
1196    start=0.12,
1197    pad=0.02,
1198    colorbar=False,
1199    colorbar_label=None,
1200    palette=None,
1201    norm=None,
1202    zorder=1.0,
1203    coords=None,
1204    **kwargs,
1205):
1206    """Draw one concentric ring of per-tip ``field`` values around a tree.
1207
1208    The ring is an annulus centred on the origin whose segments are coloured by
1209    each tip's ``field`` value.  Continuous values map through ``cmap`` (add a
1210    colourbar with ``colorbar=True``); categorical values use a discrete palette.
1211
1212    Rings are stacked outward: the first ring starts at the tree's outer tip
1213    radius (``start`` gap beyond it), and each subsequent ring is drawn farther
1214    out.  Returns ``(mappable_or_None, legend_handles)``.
1215    """
1216    import matplotlib
1217    import numpy as np
1218    from matplotlib.patches import Wedge
1219
1220    if ax is None:
1221        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
1222
1223        ax = plt.gca()
1224    if coords is None:
1225        coords = tree_coords(tree, layout=layout)
1226    tips = tree.get_tips()
1227    values = {t.name: t.get_data(field) for t in tips}
1228    known = {k: v for k, v in values.items() if v is not None}
1229    if not known:
1230        return None, []
1231    sectors = _tip_sectors(tree, layout, coords)
1232    base_outer = max(math.hypot(*coords[t]) for t in tips) or 1.0
1233    outer = getattr(ax, "_treeio_ring_r", base_outer + start)
1234    w = ring_width
1235    numeric = all(isinstance(v, (int, float)) for v in known.values())
1236    if numeric and not discrete:
1237        arr = np.array(
1238            [
1239                float(values[t.name]) if values[t.name] is not None else np.nan
1240                for t in tips
1241            ]
1242        )
1243        lo = float(np.nanmin(arr))
1244        hi = float(np.nanmax(arr))
1245        if not np.isfinite(lo) or lo == hi:
1246            lo, hi = 0.0, 1.0
1247        if norm is None:
1248            norm = matplotlib.colors.Normalize(vmin=lo, vmax=hi)
1249        cmap_obj = matplotlib.colormaps.get_cmap(cmap)
1250        colors = cmap_obj(norm(arr))
1251        mappable = matplotlib.cm.ScalarMappable(norm=norm, cmap=cmap_obj)
1252        for i, tip in enumerate(tips):
1253            if values[tip.name] is None:
1254                continue
1255            a0, a1 = sectors[i]
1256            ax.add_patch(
1257                Wedge(
1258                    (0, 0),
1259                    outer + w,
1260                    a0,
1261                    a1,
1262                    width=w,
1263                    facecolor=colors[i],
1264                    edgecolor="none",
1265                    zorder=zorder,
1266                    **kwargs,
1267                )
1268            )
1269        ax._treeio_ring_r = outer + w + pad
1270        if colorbar:
1271            cb = ax.figure.colorbar(mappable, ax=ax, fraction=0.03, pad=0.04)
1272            cb.set_label(colorbar_label or field, fontsize=8)
1273        return mappable, None
1274    # discrete / categorical
1275    cats = sorted(set(known.values()), key=str)
1276    pal = palette or named_palette([str(c) for c in cats])
1277    for i, tip in enumerate(tips):
1278        if values[tip.name] is None:
1279            continue
1280        a0, a1 = sectors[i]
1281        ax.add_patch(
1282            Wedge(
1283                (0, 0),
1284                outer + w,
1285                a0,
1286                a1,
1287                width=w,
1288                facecolor=pal[str(values[tip.name])],
1289                edgecolor="none",
1290                zorder=zorder,
1291                **kwargs,
1292            )
1293        )
1294    ax._treeio_ring_r = outer + w + pad
1295    import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
1296
1297    handles = [mpatches.Patch(color=c, label=str(k)) for k, c in pal.items()]
1298    return None, handles

Draw one concentric ring of per-tip field values around a tree.

The ring is an annulus centred on the origin whose segments are coloured by each tip's field value. Continuous values map through cmap (add a colourbar with colorbar=True); categorical values use a discrete palette.

Rings are stacked outward: the first ring starts at the tree's outer tip radius (start gap beyond it), and each subsequent ring is drawn farther out. Returns (mappable_or_None, legend_handles).

def add_rings( tree, fields, ax=None, layout='circular', cmap='viridis', ring_width=0.06, start=0.12, pad=0.02, **kwargs): 
1301def add_rings(
1302    tree,
1303    fields,
1304    ax=None,
1305    layout="circular",
1306    cmap="viridis",
1307    ring_width=0.06,
1308    start=0.12,
1309    pad=0.02,
1310    **kwargs,
1311):
1312    """Draw several concentric ``fields`` rings around a tree.
1313
1314    ``fields`` is a list of field names; the first is drawn innermost.
1315    ``cmap`` may be a single name or a list matching ``fields``.  Returns ``ax``.
1316    """
1317    if isinstance(cmap, (list, tuple)):
1318        assert len(cmap) == len(fields), "cmap list must match fields"
1319        cmaps = list(cmap)
1320    else:
1321        cmaps = [cmap] * len(fields)
1322    # reset the stacking anchor for each call
1323    if hasattr(ax, "_treeio_ring_r"):
1324        del ax._treeio_ring_r
1325    for f, cm in zip(fields, cmaps):
1326        add_ring(
1327            tree,
1328            f,
1329            ax=ax,
1330            layout=layout,
1331            cmap=cm,
1332            ring_width=ring_width,
1333            start=start,
1334            pad=pad,
1335            **kwargs,
1336        )
1337    return ax

Draw several concentric fields rings around a tree.

fields is a list of field names; the first is drawn innermost. cmap may be a single name or a list matching fields. Returns ax.

def add_scalebar( ax, coords, unit: float | None = None, label: str = 'branch length', loc: tuple[float, float] | None = None): 
1897def add_scalebar(
1898    ax,
1899    coords,
1900    unit: float | None = None,
1901    label: str = "branch length",
1902    loc: tuple[float, float] | None = None,
1903):
1904    """Draw a branch-unit scale bar in data coordinates.
1905
1906    ``coords`` is the node -> ``(x, y)`` mapping from :func:`tree_coords`.
1907    """
1908
1909    xs = [c[0] for c in coords.values()]
1910    ys = [c[1] for c in coords.values()]
1911    lo_x, hi_x = min(xs), max(xs)
1912    lo_y, hi_y = min(ys), max(ys)
1913    span = (hi_x - lo_x) or 1.0
1914    if unit is None:
1915        unit = _nice_unit(span / 5.0)
1916    if loc is None:
1917        x0 = lo_x + 0.02 * span
1918        y0 = hi_y + 0.04 * (hi_y - lo_y + 1.0)
1919    else:
1920        x0, y0 = loc
1921    ax.plot([x0, x0 + unit], [y0, y0], color="#333333", lw=1.2)
1922    h = 0.02 * (hi_y - lo_y + 1.0)
1923    ax.plot([x0, x0], [y0 - h, y0 + h], color="#333333", lw=1.2)
1924    ax.plot([x0 + unit, x0 + unit], [y0 - h, y0 + h], color="#333333", lw=1.2)
1925    ax.text(
1926        x0 + unit / 2,
1927        y0 + 0.03 * (hi_y - lo_y + 1.0),
1928        _fmt_num(unit),
1929        ha="center",
1930        va="bottom",
1931        fontsize=8,
1932        color="#333333",
1933    )
1934    if label:
1935        ax.text(
1936            x0, y0 - 1.2 * h, label, ha="left", va="top", fontsize=8, color="#333333"
1937        )
1938    return ax

Draw a branch-unit scale bar in data coordinates.

coords is the node -> (x, y) mapping from tree_coords().

def attach( tree: Tree, data: dict[str, object] | Sequence[dict[str, object]], key: str | None = None, match: str = 'name') -> Tree: 
35def attach(
36    tree: Tree,
37    data: _Data,
38    key: str | None = None,
39    match: str = "name",
40) -> Tree:
41    """Attach external data to the nodes of ``tree``.
42
43    ``data`` may be one of:
44
45    * a ``dict`` ``{label: value}``
46    * a list of ``dict`` rows where each row has a label column and value(s)
47    * a ``dict`` ``{label: {attr: value}}`` for multi-attribute rows
48
49    ``key`` names the attribute to store a scalar value under (ignored for
50    dict rows that supply their own attribute names).  ``match`` selects the
51    node attribute to match on (``'name'`` for tips/internal labels).
52
53    Returns ``tree`` for chaining.
54    """
55    index = tree.label_index()
56    if isinstance(data, dict):
57        for label, value in data.items():
58            node = index.get(str(label))
59            if node is None:
60                continue
61            if isinstance(value, dict):
62                for k, v in value.items():
63                    node.set_data(k, v)
64            elif key is not None:
65                node.set_data(key, value)
66            else:
67                # store under its own name as attribute
68                node.set_data(str(label), value)
69    elif isinstance(data, (list, tuple)):
70        for row in data:
71            if not isinstance(row, dict):
72                continue
73            label = row.get(match) or row.get("name") or row.get("id")
74            if label is None:
75                continue
76            node = index.get(str(label))
77            if node is None:
78                continue
79            for k, v in row.items():
80                if k != match and k not in ("name", "id"):
81                    node.set_data(k, v)
82    else:
83        raise TypeError(f"unsupported data type {type(data).__name__}")
84    return tree

Attach external data to the nodes of tree.

data may be one of:

  • a dict {label: value}
  • a list of dict rows where each row has a label column and value(s)
  • a dict {label: {attr: value}} for multi-attribute rows

key names the attribute to store a scalar value under (ignored for dict rows that supply their own attribute names). match selects the node attribute to match on ('name' for tips/internal labels).

Returns tree for chaining.

def build_tree( sequences: dict[str, str] | Sequence[str] | Sequence[tuple[str, str]], model: str = 'p', rooted: bool = True) -> Tree: 
243def build_tree(
244    sequences: _SeqInput,
245    model: str = "p",
246    rooted: bool = True,
247) -> Tree:
248    """Build a Tree from an alignment / sequences using distance + neighbour joining.
249
250    ``sequences`` may be a ``{name: sequence}`` dict, an iterable of
251    ``(name, sequence)`` pairs, a list of raw sequence strings, or Biopython
252    ``SeqRecord`` objects.  Sequences must be aligned (equal length).
253
254    ``model`` selects the distance model (``"p"`` or ``"jc"`` / ``"jc69"``).
255    Returns a :class:`Tree`.
256    """
257    labels, matrix = distance_matrix(sequences, model=model)
258    tree = neighbor_joining(labels, matrix)
259    if not rooted:
260        tree.unroot()
261    return tree

55    """Build a deterministic ``{name: hex}`` palette from a value mapping.
56
57    Numeric values map to a continuous viridis gradient; categorical values
58    cycle through a discrete palette.
59    """
60    items = [(k, v) for k, v in values.items() if v is not None]
61    if not items:
62        return {}
63    numeric = [v for _, v in items if isinstance(v, (int, float))]
64    if len(numeric) == len(items):
65        lo, hi = min(numeric), max(numeric)
66        span = (hi - lo) or 1.0
67        return {name: _gradient((v - lo) / span) for name, v in items}
68    cats = {}
69    out = {}
70    for name, v in items:
71        key = str(v)
72        if key not in cats:
73            cats[key] = _PALETTE[len(cats) % len(_PALETTE)]
74        out[name] = cats[key]
75    return out

def detect_format(source: str) -> str: 
122def detect_format(source: str) -> str:
123    """Best-effort detection of the tree format of ``source``."""
124    s = source.lstrip()
125    if s.startswith("#NEXUS"):
126        # only call it MrBayes when there is an actual ``begin mrbayes`` block
127        if _MRBAYES_RE.search(s):
128            return "mrbayes"
129        return "nexus"
130    # Determine the root element's *local* name across an optional ``<?xml?>``
131    # declaration, leading markup (comments / DOCTYPE) and a namespace prefix
132    # (e.g. ``<ns0:nexml>``).  The old ``startswith("<nexml")`` check missed a
133    # declaration or a prefixed root, letting NeXML fall through to ``phyloxml``.
134    decl = _XML_DECL_RE.match(s)
135    if decl:
136        s = s[decl.end() :].lstrip()
137    tag_m = _ROOT_TAG_RE.match(s)
138    root_local = tag_m.group(2) if tag_m else None
139    if root_local == "nexml":
140        return "nexml"
141    if root_local == "phyloxml":
142        return "phyloxml"
143    if s.startswith(("<?xml", "<")):
144        return "phyloxml"
145    if s[:1] in ("{", "["):
146        # Structured JSON.  Inspect the parsed top-level structure rather than
147        # searching a raw substring: a one-node tree named "tree" is a JSON
148        # dict with a "name" key, and a multi-tree payload is a JSON array, so
149        # the old '"tree"' in s / leading "["==newick heuristics were wrong.
150        try:
151            data = _json.loads(s)
152        except (ValueError, TypeError):
153            data = None
154        if isinstance(data, dict) and "tree" in data:
155            # dict with a "tree" key is a Jplace placement document
156            return "jplace"
157        if isinstance(data, (dict, list)):
158            # dict -> single tree, list -> multiple trees
159            return "json"
160        if s.startswith("{"):
161            # malformed-but-JSON-looking payload, best effort
162            return "json"
163        # Unparseable "[" text (e.g. the newick [&R] root marker) falls through
164    if _PHYLIP_HEADER_RE.match(s.split("\n", 1)[0]):
165        return "phylip"
166    if s.startswith(("(", "[")):
167        # [&R] rooted marker -> newick-ish
168        return "newick"
169    return "newick"

Best-effort detection of the tree format of source.

def distance_matrix( sequences: dict[str, str] | Sequence[str] | Sequence[tuple[str, str]], model: str = 'p') -> tuple[list[str], list[list[float]]]: 
119def distance_matrix(
120    sequences: _SeqInput, model: str = "p"
121) -> tuple[list[str], list[list[float]]]:
122    """Return ``(labels, matrix)`` of pairwise distances.
123
124    ``model`` may be ``"p"`` (raw p-distance, default) or ``"jc"`` / ``"jc69"``
125    (Jukes-Cantor corrected).  All sequences must be aligned (equal length).
126    """
127    if model not in _MODELS:
128        raise ValueError(
129            f"unknown distance model {model!r}; choose from {sorted(set(_MODELS))}"
130        )
131    labels, texts = _normalise(sequences)
132    n = len(texts)
133    func = _MODELS[model]
134    matrix = [[0.0] * n for _ in range(n)]
135    for i in range(n):
136        for j in range(i + 1, n):
137            d = func(texts[i], texts[j])
138            matrix[i][j] = matrix[j][i] = d
139    return labels, matrix

Return (labels, matrix) of pairwise distances.

model may be "p" (raw p-distance, default) or "jc" / "jc69" (Jukes-Cantor corrected). All sequences must be aligned (equal length).

def draw_tree( tree: Tree, ax=None, layout: str = 'rectangular', tip_labels: bool = True, tip_points: bool = True, node_points: bool = False, node_support: bool = False, tip_colors: dict[str, str] | None = None, tip_color_field: str | None = None, show_tip_legend: bool = True, edge_color: str = '#333333', edge_width: float = 1.2, label_size: int = 10, label_radial_offset: float = 0.04, axis_label_size: int = 9, tick_size: int = 8, reverse_x: bool = False, branch_color_field: str | None = None, branch_palette: dict[str, str] | None = None, cmap: str = 'viridis', theme: str = 'clean', show_colorbar: bool = False, colorbar_label: str = 'value', use_branch_length: bool | None = None, **kwargs): 
573def draw_tree(
574    tree: Tree,
575    ax=None,
576    layout: str = "rectangular",
577    tip_labels: bool = True,
578    tip_points: bool = True,
579    node_points: bool = False,
580    node_support: bool = False,
581    tip_colors: dict[str, str] | None = None,
582    tip_color_field: str | None = None,
583    show_tip_legend: bool = True,
584    edge_color: str = "#333333",
585    edge_width: float = 1.2,
586    label_size: int = 10,
587    label_radial_offset: float = 0.04,
588    axis_label_size: int = 9,
589    tick_size: int = 8,
590    reverse_x: bool = False,
591    branch_color_field: str | None = None,
592    branch_palette: dict[str, str] | None = None,
593    cmap: str = "viridis",
594    theme: str = "clean",
595    show_colorbar: bool = False,
596    colorbar_label: str = "value",
597    use_branch_length: bool | None = None,
598    **kwargs,
599):
600    """Draw ``tree`` onto ``ax`` (creating one if ``ax`` is None) and return it.
601
602    Uses real ``ax`` primitives (``LineCollection`` + ``scatter`` + ``text``)
603    so the returned axes is fully matplotlib-compatible.  Edges are batched
604    into a single collection and all tips into one ``scatter``, so very large
605    trees render quickly.
606
607    ``branch_color_field`` colours each branch by a per-node value and adds a
608    continuous colourbar if ``show_colorbar`` is true; ``theme`` applies a
609    :func:`tree_theme` style.
610    """
611    plt = _mpl()
612    from matplotlib.collections import LineCollection
613
614    polar = layout in _POLAR_LAYOUTS
615    if ax is None:
616        figsize = kwargs.pop("figsize", None)
617        w, h = _figsize(tree, layout)
618        ax = plt.subplots(
619            figsize=figsize or (w / 80.0, h / 80.0),
620            subplot_kw={"aspect": "equal"} if polar else None,
621        )[1]
622    # ``use_branch_length=False`` draws a cladogram (branch.length='none'), which
623    # also fixes the "collapsed core" circular artifact seen on skewed trees by
624    # spacing tips evenly instead of scaling radius by a single longest path.
625    coords = tree_coords(
626        tree, layout=layout, reverse_x=reverse_x, use_branch_length=use_branch_length
627    )
628    segments = edge_segments(tree, coords, layout=layout)
629
630    mappable = None
631    branch_legend = None
632    if branch_color_field is not None:
633        import matplotlib
634        import numpy as np
635
636        childs = [c for c in tree.traverse("preorder") if c.parent is not None]
637        vals = [c.get_data(branch_color_field) for c in childs]
638        numeric = vals and all(
639            v is not None and isinstance(v, (int, float, np.number)) for v in vals
640        )
641        if vals and numeric:
642            arr = np.asarray(
643                [np.nan if v is None else float(v) for v in vals], dtype=float
644            )
645            if np.all(np.isnan(arr)):
646                lc = LineCollection(
647                    segments,
648                    colors=edge_color,
649                    linewidths=edge_width,
650                    capstyle="round",
651                    antialiaseds=True,
652                    zorder=1,
653                )
654            else:
655                lo = float(np.nanmin(arr))
656                hi = float(np.nanmax(arr))
657                if not np.isfinite(lo) or lo == hi:
658                    lo, hi = 0.0, 1.0
659                norm = matplotlib.colors.Normalize(vmin=lo, vmax=hi)
660                lc = LineCollection(
661                    segments,
662                    array=arr,
663                    cmap=matplotlib.colormaps.get_cmap(cmap),
664                    norm=norm,
665                    linewidths=edge_width,
666                    capstyle="round",
667                    zorder=1,
668                )
669                mappable = lc
670        else:
671            # categorical branch colouring (discrete classes drawn as solid segs)
672            alls = [str(v) for v in vals if v is not None]
673            cats = sorted(set(alls), key=str)
674            pal = branch_palette or named_palette(cats)
675            colors = [
676                pal.get(str(v), edge_color) if v is not None else edge_color
677                for v in vals
678            ]
679            lc = LineCollection(
680                segments,
681                colors=colors,
682                linewidths=edge_width,
683                capstyle="round",
684                antialiaseds=True,
685                zorder=1,
686            )
687            import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
688
689            branch_legend = [(c, pal[str(c)]) for c in cats]
690    else:
691        lc = LineCollection(
692            segments,
693            colors=edge_color,
694            linewidths=edge_width,
695            capstyle="round",
696            antialiaseds=True,
697            zorder=1,
698        )
699    ax.add_collection(lc)
700    if branch_legend and show_tip_legend:
701        import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
702
703        handles = [mpatches.Patch(color=c, label=str(k)) for k, c in branch_legend]
704        ax.legend(
705            handles=handles,
706            title=branch_color_field,
707            fontsize=8,
708            title_fontsize=9,
709            loc="center left",
710            bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 0.5),
711        )
712
713    tips = tree.get_tips()
714    tip_x = [coords[t][0] for t in tips]
715    tip_y = [coords[t][1] for t in tips]
716    tip_c, tip_mappable, tip_legend = _tip_colors_for(
717        tree, tips, tip_colors, tip_color_field, cmap, edge_color
718    )
719    if tip_points:
720        # a single PathCollection is batched by matplotlib (already the compact
721        # representation); nothing more is needed here.
722        ax.scatter(
723            tip_x, tip_y, s=18, c=tip_c, zorder=3, edgecolors="none", linewidths=0
724        )
725    if tip_labels:
726        if polar:
727            import bisect
728            import math
729
730            n = len(tips) or 1
731            # wrap-around-safe angular crowding drives the radial offset so
732            # dense clusters push their labels outward (avoiding overlap).
733            threshold = (2 * math.pi / n) * 0.6
734            angles = [math.atan2(tip_y[i], tip_x[i]) for i in range(n)]
735            # Count, for every tip, how many other tips lie within ``threshold``
736            # radians on the circle -- the label crowd.  The naive per-tip scan is
737            # O(n^2); a 3x-periodic (shifted) copy of the sorted angles lets each
738            # count be answered with two binary searches in O(n log n) total, and
739            # yields the same integer crowd (verified bit-for-bit).  The original
740            # crowd includes the tip itself (``j`` runs over all tips).
741            ext = sorted(angles)
742            ext = [x - 2 * math.pi for x in ext] + ext + [x + 2 * math.pi for x in ext]
743            offset_map = {}
744            for i in range(n):
745                a = angles[i]
746                crowd = bisect.bisect_right(ext, a + threshold) - bisect.bisect_left(
747                    ext, a - threshold
748                )
749                offset_map[i] = label_radial_offset * (1 + 0.3 * max(0, crowd - 1))
750        else:
751            offset_map = {}
752        for i, (t, x, y, c) in enumerate(zip(tips, tip_x, tip_y, tip_c)):
753            off = offset_map.get(i, label_radial_offset)
754            _write_tip_label(ax, x, y, t.name, polar, c, label_size, offset=off)
755
756    if node_points or node_support:
757        # ``get_internal_nodes`` is a full post-order walk that wraps every node
758        # in a ``_ChildrenView``; skip it entirely on the default path where
759        # neither internal markers nor support labels are drawn.
760        nodes = tree.get_internal_nodes()
761        if node_points:
762            ax.scatter(
763                [coords[n][0] for n in nodes],
764                [coords[n][1] for n in nodes],
765                s=12,
766                c=["#999999"],
767                zorder=3,
768            )
769        if node_support:
770            for n in nodes:
771                if n.support is not None:
772                    x, y = coords[n]
773                    ax.text(
774                        x,
775                        y + 0.05,
776                        str(n.support),
777                        fontsize=label_size - 2,
778                        color="#666666",
779                        ha="center",
780                        va="bottom",
781                    )
782
783    if polar and theme == "void":
784        ax.set_axis_off()
785    elif not polar:
786        tree_theme(ax, style=theme)
787        ax.set_xlabel(
788            "branch length"
789            if any(
790                t.branch_length for t in tree.traverse("preorder") if t.branch_length
791            )
792            else "edges",
793            fontsize=axis_label_size,
794        )
795        ax.tick_params(labelsize=tick_size, direction="out")
796        if len(tips) <= 200:
797            ax.set_yticks(list(range(len(tips))))
798            ax.set_yticklabels([])
799    ax.autoscale()
800    # colourbar / legend for the tip field
801    if tip_mappable is not None and show_tip_legend:
802        cb = ax.figure.colorbar(tip_mappable, ax=ax)
803        cb.set_label(tip_color_field, fontsize=9)
804    elif tip_legend and show_tip_legend:
805        import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
806
807        handles = [mpatches.Patch(color=c, label=str(k)) for k, c in tip_legend]
808        ax.legend(
809            handles=handles,
810            title=tip_color_field,
811            fontsize=8,
812            title_fontsize=9,
813            loc="upper left",
814            bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1.0),
815        )
816    if show_colorbar and mappable is not None:
817        cb = ax.figure.colorbar(mappable, ax=ax)
818        if colorbar_label:
819            cb.set_label(colorbar_label)
820        ax._treeio_mappable = mappable
821    return ax

Uses real ax primitives (LineCollection + scatter + text) so the returned axes is fully matplotlib-compatible. Edges are batched into a single collection and all tips into one scatter, so very large trees render quickly.

branch_color_field colours each branch by a per-node value and adds a continuous colourbar if show_colorbar is true; theme applies a tree_theme() style.

def edge_segments( tree: Tree, coords=None, layout: str = 'rectangular') -> list[list[tuple[float, float]]]: 
475def edge_segments(
476    tree: Tree, coords=None, layout: str = "rectangular"
477) -> list[list[tuple[float, float]]]:
478    """Return a list of polylines (each a list of points) for every edge.
479
480    ``roundrect`` renders L-shaped phylogram edges but with rounded corners at
481    each elbow, matching the ``ggtree`` layout of the same name.  ``circular`` /
482    ``fan`` / ``radial`` / ``unrooted`` / ``slanted`` draw straight edges.
483    """
484    if coords is None:
485        coords = tree_coords(tree, layout)
486    straight = (
487        layout in _POLAR_LAYOUTS or layout == "slanted" or layout in _LAYOUT_REGISTRY
488    )
489    segs = []
490    for node in tree.traverse("preorder"):
491        if node.parent is None:
492            continue
493        xp, yp = coords[node.parent]
494        xc, yc = coords[node]
495        if straight:
496            segs.append([(xp, yp), (xc, yc)])
497        elif layout == "roundrect":
498            segs.append(_rounded_lpath(xp, yp, xc, yc))
499        else:
500            segs.append([(xp, yp), (xp, yc), (xc, yc)])
501    return segs

Return a list of polylines (each a list of points) for every edge.

roundrect renders L-shaped phylogram edges but with rounded corners at each elbow, matching the ggtree layout of the same name. circular / fan / radial / unrooted / slanted draw straight edges.

def facet_grid( tree: Tree, *fields: str, layout: str = 'rectangular', figsize=None, cmap: str = 'viridis', tip_labels: bool = True, share_y: bool = True, shared_legend: bool = True): 
1941def facet_grid(
1942    tree: Tree,
1943    *fields: str,
1944    layout: str = "rectangular",
1945    figsize=None,
1946    cmap: str = "viridis",
1947    tip_labels: bool = True,
1948    share_y: bool = True,
1949    shared_legend: bool = True,
1950):
1951    """Draw a tree on the left and one per-tip data panel per ``field`` on the right.
1952
1953    Returns the matplotlib ``Figure``.  Tips are aligned across panels.  When
1954    ``shared_legend`` is true a single colourbar / categorical legend is drawn
1955    at the figure edge.
1956    """
1957    import matplotlib
1958    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
1959    import numpy as np
1960    from matplotlib.collections import LineCollection
1961
1962    fields = list(fields)
1963    ncols = 1 + len(fields)
1964    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
1965        1, ncols, figsize=figsize or ((4 + 2 * len(fields)), 6), sharey=share_y
1966    )
1967    axes = list(axes) if ncols > 1 else [axes]
1968    coords = tree_coords(tree, layout=layout)
1969    tips = tree.get_tips()
1970    tip_y = [coords[t][1] for t in tips]
1971
1972    # left panel: the tree
1973    tree_ax = axes[0]
1974    segs = edge_segments(tree, coords, layout=layout)
1975    tree_ax.add_collection(LineCollection(segs, colors="#333333", linewidths=1.2))
1976    tree_ax.scatter([coords[t][0] for t in tips], tip_y, s=14, c="#333333", zorder=3)
1977    if tip_labels:
1978        for t, x, y in zip(tips, [coords[t][0] for t in tips], tip_y):
1979            tree_ax.text(x, y, t.name, fontsize=8, va="center")
1980    tree_ax.set_ylabel("tree" if layout in ("circular", "unrooted") else "")
1981    tree_ax.autoscale()
1982
1983    widths = 0.6
1984    legend = []
1985    for i, field in enumerate(fields):
1986        pax = axes[i + 1]
1987        values = {t.name: t.get_data(field) for t in tips}
1988        known = {k: v for k, v in values.items() if v is not None}
1989        numeric = bool(known) and all(
1990            isinstance(v, (int, float)) for v in known.values()
1991        )
1992        if numeric:
1993            arr = np.array(
1994                [
1995                    float(values[t.name]) if values[t.name] is not None else np.nan
1996                    for t in tips
1997                ]
1998            )
1999            lo = float(np.nanmin(arr))
2000            hi = float(np.nanmax(arr))
2001            if not np.isfinite(lo) or lo == hi:
2002                lo, hi = 0.0, 1.0
2003            norm = matplotlib.colors.Normalize(vmin=lo, vmax=hi)
2004            colors = matplotlib.colormaps.get_cmap(cmap)(norm(arr))
2005        else:
2006            uniq = {v: i for i, v in enumerate(sorted(set(known.values()), key=str))}
2007            pal = named_palette([str(c) for c in uniq])
2008            colors = [pal.get(str(values[t.name]), "#cccccc") for t in tips]
2009            if shared_legend:
2010                legend.extend((c, pal[str(c)]) for c in uniq)
2011        # draw one rectangle per tip
2012        for j, (t, y) in enumerate(zip(tips, tip_y)):
2013            pax.add_patch(
2014                plt.Rectangle(
2015                    (0, y - widths / 2),
2016                    widths,
2017                    widths,
2018                    facecolor=colors[j],
2019                    edgecolor="none",
2020                )
2021            )
2022        pax.set_xlim(0, widths)
2023        pax.set_ylim(min(tip_y) - 0.6, max(tip_y) + 0.6)
2024        pax.set_title(field, fontsize=9)
2025        pax.spines["top"].set_visible(False)
2026        pax.spines["right"].set_visible(False)
2027        pax.set_xticks([])
2028        pax.set_yticks([])
2029
2030    # one shared colourbar at the right edge (first continuous field)
2031    if shared_legend and fields:
2032        first = fields[0]
2033        values = {t.name: t.get_data(first) for t in tips}
2034        known = {k: v for k, v in values.items() if v is not None}
2035        if known and all(isinstance(v, (int, float)) for v in known.values()):
2036            arr = np.array(
2037                [
2038                    float(values[t.name]) if values[t.name] is not None else np.nan
2039                    for t in tips
2040                ]
2041            )
2042            lo = float(np.nanmin(arr))
2043            hi = float(np.nanmax(arr))
2044            if not np.isfinite(lo) or lo == hi:
2045                lo, hi = 0.0, 1.0
2046            norm = matplotlib.colors.Normalize(vmin=lo, vmax=hi)
2047            mappable = matplotlib.cm.ScalarMappable(
2048                norm=norm, cmap=matplotlib.colormaps.get_cmap(cmap)
2049            )
2050            cb = fig.colorbar(mappable, ax=axes[-1], fraction=0.03, pad=0.04)
2051            cb.ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)
2052            cb.set_label(first, fontsize=8)
2053        elif legend:
2054            import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
2055
2056            seen = set()
2057            handles = [
2058                mpatches.Patch(color=c, label=str(k))
2059                for k, c in legend
2060                if not (k in seen or seen.add(k))
2061            ]
2062            if handles:
2063                fig.legend(
2064                    handles=handles,
2065                    loc="center left",
2066                    bbox_to_anchor=(1.0, 0.5),
2067                    fontsize=8,
2068                )
2069
2070    fig.tight_layout()

def fortify(tree: Tree, layout: str = 'rectangular') -> list[dict]: 
1393def fortify(tree: Tree, layout: str = "rectangular") -> list[dict]:
1394    """Return the tree as a list of node records (a data-frame style table).
1395
1396    Columns
1397    -------
1398    id, parent, label, is_tip, branch_length, support, x, y
1399    plus every per-node annotation attribute.
1400
1401    ``layout`` accepts ``rectangular`` / ``circular`` to choose how ``x`` and
1402    ``y`` are computed.  This mirrors the standard
1403    ``fortify``.
1404    """
1405    # compute x/y coordinates (rectangular layout by default)
1406    tree.get_y_and_x(x_as_branch=True)
1407    index = tree.get_node2index()
1408    rows: list[dict] = []
1409    for node in tree.traverse("postorder"):
1410        row = {
1411            "id": index[node],
1412            "parent": index.get(node.parent),
1413            "label": node.name,
1414            "is_tip": node.is_leaf(),
1415            "branch_length": node.branch_length,
1416            "support": node.support,
1417            "x": float(getattr(node, "_x", 0.0)),
1418            "y": float(getattr(node, "_y", 0.0)),
1419        }
1420        # append per-node annotation attributes
1421        for key, value in _iter_attrs(node):
1422            if key not in row:
1423                row[key] = value
1424        rows.append(row)
1425    return rows

def gheatmap( tree, columns, ax=None, layout='rectangular', cmap='viridis', discrete=False, cell_width=0.8, cell_gap=0.0, group_gap=0.4, group_by=None, tip_labels=False, label_size=9, colorbar=False, colorbar_label='value', palette=None, zorder=2.0, coords=None, **kwargs): 
1340def gheatmap(
1341    tree,
1342    columns,
1343    ax=None,
1344    layout="rectangular",
1345    cmap="viridis",
1346    discrete=False,
1347    cell_width=0.8,
1348    cell_gap=0.0,
1349    group_gap=0.4,
1350    group_by=None,
1351    tip_labels=False,
1352    label_size=9,
1353    colorbar=False,
1354    colorbar_label="value",
1355    palette=None,
1356    zorder=2.0,
1357    coords=None,
1358    **kwargs,
1359):
1360    """Draw a per-tip heatmap matrix beside a tree (``gheatmap`` analogue).
1361
1362    ``columns`` is a list of field names attached to tips; each is one column
1363    (rectangular layout) or one concentric ring (circular layout).  In the
1364    rectangular layout the tree is drawn first and the coloured matrix is placed
1365    immediately to its right, one row per tip, with optional gaps between
1366    ``group_by`` column groups.  Returns ``(ax, column_specs)`` where
1367    ``column_specs`` holds each column's left edge (rectangular) so the caller
1368    can draw column-axis labels.
1369
1370    Continuous values share a single ``cmap``/norm across all columns;
1371    categorical values use a discrete palette (``discrete=True``).
1372    """
1373    import matplotlib
1374    import numpy as np
1375    from matplotlib.patches import Rectangle, Wedge
1376
1377    if ax is None:
1378        import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
1379
1380        ax = plt.gca()
1381    if coords is None:
1382        coords = tree_coords(tree, layout=layout)
1383    tips = tree.get_tips()
1384    # gather per-column values (aligned to tips; missing -> None)
1385    allvals = []
1386    numeric = True
1387    cats = set()
1388    for col in columns:
1389        vals = {t.name: t.get_data(col) for t in tips}
1390        allvals.append(vals)
1391        known = [v for v in vals.values() if v is not None]
1392        if not known:
1393            continue
1394        if not all(isinstance(v, (int, float, np.number)) for v in known):
1395            numeric = False
1396        cats.update(str(v) for v in known)
1397    if numeric and not discrete:
1398        # shared continuous colour scale
1399        known = [float(v) for vals in allvals for v in vals.values() if v is not None]
1400        lo = min(known) if known else 0.0
1401        hi = max(known) if known else 1.0
1402        if not np.isfinite(lo) or lo == hi:
1403            lo, hi = 0.0, 1.0
1404        norm = matplotlib.colors.Normalize(vmin=lo, vmax=hi)
1405        cmap_obj = matplotlib.colormaps.get_cmap(cmap)
1406        mappable = matplotlib.cm.ScalarMappable(norm=norm, cmap=cmap_obj)
1407        colfunc = lambda v: cmap_obj(norm(float(v)))
1408    else:
1409        cats = sorted(cats, key=str)
1410        pal = palette or named_palette(cats)
1411        mappable = None
1412        colfunc = lambda v: pal[str(v)]
1413
1414    if layout in ("circular", "fan", "radial", "unrooted"):
1415        # concentric rings -- each column is drawn at a progressively larger radius
1416        base_outer = max(math.hypot(*coords[t]) for t in tips) or 1.0
1417        w = cell_width / 8.0
1418        sectors = _tip_sectors(tree, layout, coords)
1419        for vals in allvals:
1420            outer = getattr(ax, "_treeio_ring_r", base_outer + 0.12)
1421            for i, tip in enumerate(tips):
1422                v = vals.get(tip.name)
1423                if v is None:
1424                    continue
1425                a0, a1 = sectors[i]
1426                ax.add_patch(
1427                    Wedge(
1428                        (0, 0),
1429                        outer + w,
1430                        a0,
1431                        a1,
1432                        width=w,
1433                        facecolor=colfunc(v),
1434                        edgecolor="none",
1435                        zorder=zorder,
1436                    )
1437                )
1438            ax._treeio_ring_r = outer + w + 0.02
1439        if colorbar and mappable is not None:
1440            cb = ax.figure.colorbar(mappable, ax=ax, fraction=0.03, pad=0.04)
1441            cb.set_label(colorbar_label, fontsize=8)
1442        return ax, None
1443
1444    # rectangular: draw the matrix to the right of the tips
1445    tip_y = [coords[t][1] for t in tips]
1446    x0 = max(coords[t][0] for t in tips)
1447    left = x0 + 0.05 * max(abs(x0), 1.0)
1448    specs = []
1449    len(columns)
1450    for ci, vals in enumerate(allvals):
1451        # group separator
1452        if group_by and ci > 0 and group_by[ci - 1] is not None:
1453            left += group_gap
1454        w = cell_width
1455        specs.append({"left": left, "width": w, "field": columns[ci]})
1456        for i, tip in enumerate(tips):
1457            v = vals.get(tip.name)
1458            if v is None:
1459                continue
1460            ax.add_patch(
1461                Rectangle(
1462                    (left, tip_y[i] - 0.4),
1463                    w,
1464                    0.8,
1465                    facecolor=colfunc(v),
1466                    edgecolor="none",
1467                    zorder=zorder,
1468                )
1469            )
1470        left += w + cell_gap
1471    if tip_labels:
1472        for i, tip in enumerate(tips):
1473            ax.text(
1474                left + 0.6,
1475                tip_y[i],
1476                tip.name,
1477                fontsize=label_size,
1478                va="center",
1479                ha="left",
1480            )
1481    if colorbar and mappable is not None:
1482        cb = ax.figure.colorbar(mappable, ax=ax, fraction=0.03, pad=0.04)
1483        cb.set_label(colorbar_label, fontsize=8)
1484    ax.set_xlim((-0.05 * max(abs(x0), 1.0), left + (cell_width if tip_labels else 0)))
1485    return ax, specs

columns is a list of field names attached to tips; each is one column (rectangular layout) or one concentric ring (circular layout). In the rectangular layout the tree is drawn first and the coloured matrix is placed immediately to its right, one row per tip, with optional gaps between group_by column groups. Returns (ax, column_specs) where column_specs holds each column's left edge (rectangular) so the caller can draw column-axis labels.

def grid_of_trees( trees, labels=None, layout: str = 'rectangular', figsize=None, share_y: bool = True, tip_labels: bool = True, ncols: int | None = None, layouts=None, **kwargs): 
2074def grid_of_trees(
2075    trees,
2076    labels=None,
2077    layout: str = "rectangular",
2078    figsize=None,
2079    share_y: bool = True,
2080    tip_labels: bool = True,
2081    ncols: int | None = None,
2082    layouts=None,
2083    **kwargs,
2084):
2085    """Plot several trees in a grid sharing the y (tip) axis.
2086
2087    Trees are arranged left-to-right (or wrapped to ``ncols`` columns); when
2088    ``share_y`` is true the tip y-axis is shared so tips align across panels.
2089    ``layouts`` may be a list giving the layout of each tree.  Returns the
2090    matplotlib ``Figure``.
2091    """
2092    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
2093
2094    trees = list(trees)
2095    if not trees:
2096        raise ValueError("no trees given")
2097    n = len(trees)
2098    if ncols is None:
2099        ncols = n
2100    nrows = (n + ncols - 1) // ncols
2101    fig, axes = plt.subplots(
2102        nrows,
2103        ncols,
2104        figsize=figsize or (5 * ncols, 6 * nrows),
2105        sharey=share_y,
2106        squeeze=False,
2107    )
2108    max_tips = max(t.nleaves for t in trees)
2109    flat = axes.flatten()
2110    for i, t in enumerate(trees):
2111        ax = flat[i]
2112        lay = layouts[i] if layouts else layout
2113        draw_tree(t, ax=ax, layout=lay, tip_labels=tip_labels, tick_size=7, **kwargs)
2114        if labels is not None:
2115            ax.set_title(labels[i] if i < len(labels) else f"tree {i + 1}", fontsize=10)
2116        if share_y:
2117            ax.set_ylim(-0.5, max_tips - 0.5)
2118    for j in range(n, len(flat)):
2119        flat[j].set_axis_off()
2120    if share_y:
2121        flat[0].set_yticks([])
2122        flat[0].set_ylabel("")
2123    fig.tight_layout()
2124    return fig

def highlight_clade( tree, clade, ax=None, layout='rectangular', fill='#2e8b57', alpha=0.35, edgecolor='none', lw=0, zorder=0.6, pad=0.45, coords=None, extend_center=False, **kwargs): 
1020def highlight_clade(
1021    tree,
1022    clade,
1023    ax=None,
1024    layout="rectangular",
1025    fill="#2e8b57",
1026    alpha=0.35,
1027    edgecolor="none",
1028    lw=0,
1029    zorder=0.6,
1030    pad=0.45,
1031    coords=None,
1032    extend_center=False,
1033    **kwargs,
1034):
1035    """Shade the region behind a clade (``geom_hilight`` analogue).
1036
1037    ``clade`` may be a :class:`Tree` node, a node name, or an iterable of tip
1038    names (their MRCA).  Rectangular layouts draw a filled rectangle covering
1039    the clade tips; polar layouts draw an annular wedge.  Returns the patch.
1040    """
1041    import matplotlib.patches as mpatches
1042    import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
1043
1044    if ax is None:
1045        ax = plt.gca()
1046    if isinstance(clade, str):
1047        clade = tree.get_node_by_label(clade) or tree.get_tip_by_label(clade)
1048    elif isinstance(clade, (list, tuple, set)):
1049        clade = tree.get_mrca(*list(clade))
1050    if clade is None:
1051        raise ValueError("clade not found in tree")
1052    if coords is None:
1053        coords = tree_coords(tree, layout=layout)
1054    b = _clade_bounds(tree, coords, clade, layout)
1055    if b is None:
1056        return None
1057    if layout in _POLAR_LAYOUTS:
1058        r0, r1, a0, a1 = b
1059        if r1 <= r0:
1060            r1 = r0 + 1e-3
1061        if extend_center:
1062            # full-sector wedge from the origin out to the clade's tip radius
1063            patch = mpatches.Wedge(
1064                (0, 0),
1065                r1,
1066                a0,
1067                a1,
1068                facecolor=fill,
1069                alpha=alpha,
1070                edgecolor=edgecolor,
1071                linewidth=lw,
1072                zorder=zorder,
1073                **kwargs,
1074            )
1075        else:
1076            patch = mpatches.Wedge(
1077                (0, 0),
1078                r1,
1079                a0,
1080                a1,
1081                width=r1 - r0,
1082                facecolor=fill,
1083                alpha=alpha,
1084                edgecolor=edgecolor,
1085                linewidth=lw,
1086                zorder=zorder,
1087                **kwargs,
1088            )
1089    else:
1090        x0, x1, y0, y1 = b
1091        # box starts at the clade's split node (x0), extends past its tips
1092        left = x0
1093        right = x1 + 0.02 * max(abs(x1), 1.0)
1094        patch = mpatches.Rectangle(
1095            (left, y0 - pad),
1096            right - left,
1097            (y1 - y0) + 2 * pad,
1098            facecolor=fill,
1099            alpha=alpha,
1100            edgecolor=edgecolor,
1101            linewidth=lw,
1102            zorder=zorder,
1103            **kwargs,
1104        )
1105    ax.add_patch(patch)
1106    return patch

def neighbor_joining( labels: Sequence[str], matrix: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> Tree: 
170def neighbor_joining(labels: Sequence[str], matrix: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) -> Tree:
171    """Build a Tree from a pairwise distance matrix using neighbour joining.
172
173    ``labels`` are the taxon names, ``matrix`` is a symmetric distance matrix.
174    Returns a (rooted) :class:`Tree` whose internal nodes are unnamed and whose
175    branch lengths come from the NJ limb-length estimates.
176    """
177    n = len(labels)
178    if len(matrix) != n or any(len(row) != n for row in matrix):
179        raise ValueError("distance matrix must be n x n for the given labels")
180    if n == 1:
181        return Tree(name=labels[0])
182
183    active = list(range(n))
184    nodes = [Tree(name=labels[i]) for i in range(n)]
185    dist = [[float(matrix[i][j]) for j in range(n)] for i in range(n)]
186
187    while len(active) > 1:
188        m = len(active)
189        if m == 2:
190            i, j = active
191            half = dist[i][j] / 2.0
192            nodes[i].branch_length = half
193            nodes[j].branch_length = half
194            root = Tree()
195            root.append_child(nodes[i])
196            root.append_child(nodes[j])
197            return _order_by_labels(root, labels)
198
199        # row sums over the active set
200        row_sum = {a: sum(dist[a][b] for b in active) for a in active}
201        # Q matrix, pick min pair
202        best = None
203        for x in range(m):
204            for y in range(x + 1, m):
205                a, b = active[x], active[y]
206                q = (m - 2) * dist[a][b] - row_sum[a] - row_sum[b]
207                if best is None or q < best[0]:
208                    best = (q, a, b)
209        _, i, j = best
210
211        limb_i = 0.5 * dist[i][j] + (row_sum[i] - row_sum[j]) / (2.0 * (m - 2))
212        limb_j = dist[i][j] - limb_i
213
214        u = Tree()
215        nodes[i].branch_length = limb_i
216        nodes[j].branch_length = limb_j
217        u.append_child(nodes[i])
218        u.append_child(nodes[j])
219
220        # new active clusters (drop i, j; add the new internal node u)
221        new_active = [a for a in active if a not in (i, j)]
222        size = len(new_active) + 1
223        new_dist = [[0.0] * size for _ in range(size)]
224        for x, a in enumerate(new_active):
225            for y, b in enumerate(new_active):
226                if a != b:
227                    new_dist[x][y] = new_dist[y][x] = dist[a][b]
228            # distance from the new cluster u to each remaining cluster
229            d = 0.5 * (dist[i][a] + dist[j][a] - dist[i][j])
230            new_dist[x][-1] = new_dist[-1][x] = d
231
232        active = list(range(size))
233        dist = new_dist
234        nodes = [nodes[a] for a in new_active] + [u]
235
236    # unreachable for n>=2 (loop always returns at m==2)
237    raise RuntimeError("unexpected neighbour-joining state")

Build a Tree from a pairwise distance matrix using neighbour joining.

labels are the taxon names, matrix is a symmetric distance matrix. Returns a (rooted) Tree whose internal nodes are unnamed and whose branch lengths come from the NJ limb-length estimates.

178    """Read a tree from a file path or raw string.

180    If ``source`` is an existing file path it is read from disc; otherwise the
181    string is treated as the tree payload itself.  Returns the first tree.
182    Passing an already-parsed :class:`Tree` is a no-op (returns it unchanged).

33    """Parse a Jplace document and return the reference Tree.

35    The parsed placements (a ``list`` keyed by placement) are stored on the
36    tree as ``tree.placements`` (a dict with ``fields``, ``placements``,
37    ``metadata`` and ``version``), so downstream code can inspect or plot
38    them without losing the raw data.
39    """

def read_json( json_string: str, name_key='name', child_key='children', branch_length_key='branch_length', support_key='support') -> list[Tree]: 
17def read_json(
18    json_string: str,
19    name_key="name",
20    child_key="children",
21    branch_length_key="branch_length",
22    support_key="support",
23) -> list[Tree]:
24    """Return a json object in the format desribed below
25
26    ```json
27    {
28      "name": "root",
29      "branch_length": 0,
30      "children": [
31        {
32          "name": "unknown",
33          "branch_length": 0.846,
34          "children": [
35            { "name": "raccoon", "branch_length": 19.19959 },
36            { "name": "bear", "branch_length": 6.80041 }
37          ]
38        },
39        {
40          "name": "unknown",
41          "branch_length": 3.87382,
42          "children": [
43
44          ...
45
46          ]
47        },
48        { "name": "dog", "branch_length": 25.46154 }
49      ]
50    }
51    ```
52    """
53
54    data = json.loads(json_string)
55
56    tree_scratch = Tree("scratch")
57
58    # Build the tree iteratively with an explicit stack so a very deep tree
59    # does not exhaust Python's recursion limit (stateful DFS over ``(obj,parent)``
60    # pairs).  This reproduces exactly what the recursive ``_parse_node`` did.
61    stack = [(data, tree_scratch)]
62    while stack:
63        obj, tree_cur = stack.pop()
64        if isinstance(obj, dict):
65            node = Tree(
66                name=obj.get(name_key),
67                branch_length=obj.get(branch_length_key),
68                support=obj.get(support_key),
69            )
70            # restore any per-node annotation (everything that is not one of
71            # the structural keys), so ``write_json``/``read_json`` round-trips
72            # ``set_data`` values.
73            structural = {name_key, branch_length_key, support_key, child_key}
74            for k, v in obj.items():
75                if k not in structural:
76                    node.set_data(k, v)
77            tree_cur._children.append(node)
78            node._parent = tree_cur
79            if child_key in obj:
80                stack.append((obj[child_key], node))
81        elif isinstance(obj, list):
82            # push reversed so a LIFO pop preserves the original left-to-right order
83            for item in reversed(obj):
84                stack.append((item, tree_cur))
85
86    return [t.isolated() for t in tree_scratch.children]

Return a json object in the format desribed below

{
  "name": "root",
  "branch_length": 0,
  "children": [
    {
      "name": "unknown",
      "branch_length": 0.846,

def read_newicks(nwk_string: str) -> list[Tree]: 
508def read_newicks(nwk_string: str) -> list[Tree]:
509    """Read one or more newick trees (separated by ``;``) into a list.
510
511    Leading whitespace and bracketed comments are skipped; trailing garbage is
512    ignored.  (NEXUS-structured input is not handled here -- use
513    :func:`treeio.read_nexus` for that.)
514    """
515    trees: list[Tree] = []
516    idx = 0
517    length = len(nwk_string)
518    while True:
519        parser = _NewickParser(nwk_string)
520        parser.i = idx
521        parser._skip()
522        if parser.i >= length:
523            break
524        # only start a new tree on a parenthesised group, a lone node label, or
525        # a bracketed root marker; anything else is trailing garbage -> stop.
526        head = nwk_string[parser.i : parser.i + 1]
527        if head not in ("(", "[") and not _is_number(head):
528            break
529        trees.append(parser.parse())
530        idx = parser.i
531    return trees

Read one or more newick trees (separated by ;) into a list.

Leading whitespace and bracketed comments are skipped; trailing garbage is ignored. (NEXUS-structured input is not handled here -- use treeio.read_nexus() for that.)

def read_nexuses( nexus_string: str, tree_name: str | None = None) -> list[Tree]: 
 81def read_nexuses(nexus_string: str, tree_name: str | None = None) -> list[Tree]:
 82    """Read every tree in a NEXUS string, honouring TRANSLATE and capturing
 83    embodied ``[&key=value]`` node annotations."""
 84    mapping: dict = {}
 85    trees: list[Tree] = []
 86
 87    for block in _BLOCK_RE.finditer(nexus_string):
 88        if block.group(1).upper() != "TREES":
 89            continue
 90        body = block.group(2)
 91        tm = _TRANSLATE_RE.search(body)
 92        if tm:
 93            mapping = _parse_translate(tm.group(1))
 94        for tree_match in _TREE_RE.finditer(body):
 95            name = tree_match.group(1).strip()
 96            if tree_name and name and name != tree_name:
 97                continue
 98            body_str = tree_match.group(2).strip()
 99            nwk = _substitute_translate(body_str, mapping)
100            t = read_newick(nwk, annotations=True)
101            if name:
102                # the TREE name is a file-level title, not a node label
103                t.set_data("tree_title", name)
104            trees.append(t)
105    return trees

Read every tree in a NEXUS string, honouring TRANSLATE and capturing embodied [&key=value] node annotations.

def read_phyloxmls(xml_string: str) -> list[Tree]: 
45def read_phyloxmls(xml_string: str) -> list[Tree]:
46    """Read every ``<phylogeny>`` element into a list of Trees."""
47    root = ET.fromstring(xml_string)
48    trees = []
49    for phylo in root.iter():
50        tag = _local(phylo.tag)
51        if tag == "phylogeny":
52            # The ``<phylogeny>`` element wraps exactly one real ``<clade>``;
53            # parse that child directly rather than the wrapper element itself,
54            # otherwise a spurious anonymous root node would be injected.
55            clade = next((c for c in phylo if _local(c.tag) == "clade"), None)
56            if clade is None:
57                continue
58            t = _parse_clade(clade)
59            t._is_rooted = phylo.get("rooted", "false").lower() == "true"
60            trees.append(t)
61    return trees

Read every <phylogeny> element into a list of Trees.

def render( tree: Tree, backend: str = 'mpl', layout: str = 'rectangular', path=None, savefig_kwargs=None, dpi: int = 300, format: str | None = None, tight: bool = True, **kwargs): 
1768def render(
1769    tree: Tree,
1770    backend: str = "mpl",
1771    layout: str = "rectangular",
1772    path=None,
1773    savefig_kwargs=None,
1774    dpi: int = 300,
1775    format: str | None = None,
1776    tight: bool = True,
1777    **kwargs,
1778):
1779    """One entry point, several backends.
1780
1781    ``backend`` is ``"mpl"`` (default; returns / saves a matplotlib axes) or
1782    ``"ascii"`` (returns an ASCII-art string).  If ``path`` is given the figure
1783    is written there with ``savefig`` (``dpi`` / ``format`` / ``tight`` control
1784    resolution, file format and bounding box).
1785    """
1786    backend = backend.lower().strip().lstrip("-")
1787    if backend in ("mpl", "matplotlib"):
1788        ax = draw_tree(tree, layout=layout, **kwargs)
1789        if path is not None:
1790            _apply_fast(ax)
1791            from pathlib import Path
1792
1793            Path(path).parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
1794            skw = dict(savefig_kwargs or {})
1795            skw.setdefault("bbox_inches", "tight" if tight else None)
1796            skw.setdefault("dpi", dpi)
1797            if format:
1798                skw.setdefault("format", format)
1799            ax.figure.savefig(path, **skw)
1800            return path
1801        return ax
1802    if backend in ("ascii", "text", "cli"):
1803        from .show import tree_to_ascii
1804
1805        is_compact = kwargs.pop("is_compact", False)
1806        is_pruned = kwargs.pop("is_pruned", True)
1807        return tree_to_ascii(tree, is_compact, is_pruned)
1808    custom = _BACKEND_REGISTRY.get(backend)
1809    if custom is not None:
1810        return custom(tree, layout=layout, **kwargs)
1811    raise ValueError(
1812        f"unknown backend {backend!r}; choose from 'mpl', 'ascii', or a registered backend"
1813    )

def suggest_figsize( tree: Tree, layout: str = 'rectangular', base_width: int = 800, tip_slot: int = 14) -> tuple[int, int]: 
 88def suggest_figsize(
 89    tree: Tree, layout: str = "rectangular", base_width: int = 800, tip_slot: int = 14
 90) -> tuple[int, int]:
 91    """A sensible canvas size ``(width, height)`` for a tree.
 92
 93    Height scales with the number of tips so points / labels do not overlap;
 94    polar layouts get a square canvas sized ~ sqrt(tips).
 95    """
 96    n = tree.nleaves or 1
 97    if layout in ("circular", "fan", "radial", "unrooted"):
 98        side = int(min(max(400, math.sqrt(n) * base_width / 5.0), 6000))
 99        return side, side
100    height = int(min(max(300, n * tip_slot + 80), 20000))
101    return int(base_width), height

def tree_coords( tree: Tree, layout: str = 'rectangular', reverse_x: bool = False, use_branch_length: bool | None = None) -> dict[Tree, tuple[float, float]]: 
144def tree_coords(
145    tree: Tree,
146    layout: str = "rectangular",
147    reverse_x: bool = False,
148    use_branch_length: bool | None = None,
149) -> dict[Tree, tuple[float, float]]:
150    """Return ``{node: (x, y)}`` in data coordinates for ``layout``.
151
152    Supported layouts: ``rectangular``, ``roundrect``, ``slanted``, ``ellipse``,
153    ``circular``, ``fan``, ``radial``, ``unrooted``, ``equal_angle``,
154    ``daylight`` and ``time``.  Unrecognised layouts raise ``ValueError`` (they
155    are never silently drawn as a rectangular tree).
156    """
157    if layout in _LAYOUT_REGISTRY:
158        return dict(_LAYOUT_REGISTRY[layout](tree))
159    if layout == "equal_angle":
160        return _equal_angle_coords(tree, reverse_x=reverse_x)
161    if layout == "daylight":
162        return _daylight_coords(tree, reverse_x=reverse_x)
163    if layout == "ellipse":
164        use_depth = False
165        coords = _rect_coords(
166            tree,
167            reverse_x=reverse_x,
168            use_depth=use_depth,
169            use_branch_length=use_branch_length,
170        )
171        return _polarize(coords, tree, "ellipse")
172    if layout not in _BUILTIN_LAYOUTS:
173        raise ValueError(f"unknown tree layout {layout!r}")
174    use_depth = layout == "radial"
175    coords = _rect_coords(
176        tree,
177        reverse_x=reverse_x,
178        use_depth=use_depth,
179        use_branch_length=use_branch_length,
180    )
181    if layout in ("circular", "fan", "radial", "unrooted"):
182        return _polarize(coords, tree, layout)
183    return coords

def tree_theme( ax, style: str = 'clean', grid: bool = False, spine_width: float = 0.8): 
1856def tree_theme(ax, style: str = "clean", grid: bool = False, spine_width: float = 0.8):
1857    """Apply a minimal publication theme to a tree axes.
1858
1859    ``style`` may be ``"clean"`` (no top/right spines), ``"void"``
1860    (axis off), ``"minimal"`` (only a bottom spine) or ``"plain"`` (full box).
1861    """
1862    if style == "void":
1863        ax.set_axis_off()
1864        return ax
1865    if style == "minimal":
1866        for s in ("top", "right", "left"):
1867            ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
1868        ax.spines["bottom"].set_linewidth(spine_width)
1869        ax.set_yticks([])
1870    elif style == "plain":
1871        for s in ("top", "right", "bottom", "left"):
1872            ax.spines[s].set_visible(True)
1873            ax.spines[s].set_linewidth(spine_width)
1874    else:  # clean
1875        for s in ("top", "right"):
1876            ax.spines[s].set_visible(False)
1877        for s in ("left", "bottom"):
1878            ax.spines[s].set_linewidth(spine_width)
1879    ax.grid(grid)
1880    return ax

style may be "clean" (no top/right spines), "void" (axis off), "minimal" (only a bottom spine) or "plain" (full box).

def write_json( trees, name_key='name', child_key='children', branch_length_key='branch_length', support_key='support') -> str: 
 89def write_json(
 90    trees,
 91    name_key="name",
 92    child_key="children",
 93    branch_length_key="branch_length",
 94    support_key="support",
 95) -> str:
 96    """Return a json object in the format desribed below"""
 97
 98    def _record_node(node):
 99        attr_key = ["name", "branch_length", "support"]
100        attr_values = [name_key, branch_length_key, support_key]
101
102        def build(n):
103            data = {v: _json_ok(getattr(n, k)) for k, v in zip(attr_key, attr_values)}
104            # persist every per-node ``set_data`` annotation (excluding internal
105            # underscore keys such as layout coordinates) so JSON round-trips them.
106            ann = n._annotations
107            if ann:
108                for k, v in ann.items():
109                    if k.startswith("_"):
110                        continue
111                    data[k] = _json_ok(v)
112            return data
113
114        # Build the record for ``node`` and its descendants iteratively (explicit
115        # stack) so a very deep tree does not exhaust Python's recursion limit.
116        root = build(node)
117        stack = [(node, root)]
118        while stack:
119            n, rec = stack.pop()
120            if n._children:
121                child_recs = []
122                for c in n._children:
123                    crec = build(c)
124                    child_recs.append(crec)
125                    stack.append((c, crec))
126                rec[child_key] = child_recs
127        return root
128
129    if isinstance(trees, Tree):
130        trees = [trees]
131
132    if len(trees) == 1:
133        json_string = json.dumps(_record_node(trees[0]))
134    else:
135        json_string = json.dumps([_record_node(t) for t in trees])
136    return json_string

Return a json object in the format desribed below

def write_nexml(tree: Tree, name: str = 'Tree') -> str: 
161def write_nexml(tree: Tree, name: str = "Tree") -> str:
162    """Write a :class:`Tree` as a NeXML document string."""
163    root = ET.Element(_label("nexml"))
164    root.set("xmlns", _NS)
165    root.set("xmlns:nex", _NS)
166    otus = ET.SubElement(root, _label("otus"))
167    otus.set("id", "otus1")
168    # assign otu ids to tips
169    tips = tree.get_tips()
170    otu_ids = {tip: f"otu{i + 1}" for i, tip in enumerate(tips)}
171    for tip in tips:
172        otu = ET.SubElement(otus, _label("otu"))
173        otu.set("id", otu_ids[tip])
174        otu.set("label", tip.name)
175    trees = ET.SubElement(root, _label("trees"))
176    trees.set("id", "trees1")
177    tree_el = ET.SubElement(trees, _label("tree"))
178    tree_el.set("id", name)
179    nids = {node: f"n{index}" for index, node in enumerate(tree.traverse("preorder"))}
180    # nodes: internal first then leaves / record order doesn't matter to readers
181    for node in tree.traverse("preorder"):
182        nd = ET.SubElement(tree_el, _label("node"))
183        nd.set("id", nids[node])
184        if node.is_leaf():
185            nd.set("otu", otu_ids[node])
186        # Names of root / internal nodes are not carried by an ``otu`` label, so
187        # record them as a ``<meta property="name">`` so the round-trip keeps
188        # them (the default ``unknown`` placeholder is not written).
189        if node.name and node.name != "unknown":
190            meta = ET.SubElement(nd, _label("meta"))
191            meta.set("property", "name")
192            meta.set("content", str(node.name))
193        if node.support is not None:
194            meta = ET.SubElement(nd, _label("meta"))
195            meta.set("property", "support")
196            meta.set("content", _fmt(node.support))
197        # Per-node annotations (set via ``set_data``) become ``<meta property=...>``
198        # so the reader (which captures any such meta back into the node) preserves
199        # them through a write(nexml)->read(nexml) round-trip.  ``name`` is already
200        # written above and ``_``-prefixed layout coords / ``None`` values are skipped.
201        if node._annotations:
202            for key, value in node._annotations.items():
203                if key == "name" or key.startswith("_"):
204                    continue
205                content = _meta_content(value)
206                if content is None:
207                    continue
208                meta = ET.SubElement(nd, _label("meta"))
209                meta.set("property", key)
210                meta.set("content", content)
211        # The root has no parent edge, so its branch_length would be dropped by the
212        # edge-emission loop below; record it as a ``<branch_length>`` child that the
213        # reader picks up directly from the node element.
214        if node.parent is None and node.branch_length is not None:
215            bl = ET.SubElement(nd, _label("branch_length"))
216            bl.text = repr(node.branch_length)
217    for node in tree.traverse("preorder"):
218        if node.parent is None:
219            continue
220        edge = ET.SubElement(tree_el, _label("edge"))
221        edge.set("id", "e" + nids[node])
222        edge.set("source", nids[node.parent])
223        edge.set("target", nids[node])
224        if node.branch_length is not None:
225            edge.set("length", repr(node.branch_length))
226    rt = ET.SubElement(tree_el, _label("root"))
227    rt.set("id", nids[tree])
228    ET.indent(root)
229    return ET.tostring(root, encoding="unicode") + "\n"

Write a Tree as a NeXML document string.

def write_nexus(trees, title: str = 'Tree') -> str: 
108def write_nexus(trees, title: str = "Tree") -> str:
109    """Write one or more trees as a NEXUS file with a TAXA + TREES block.
110
111    ``trees`` may be a single :class:`Tree` or a list of them.
112    """
113    if isinstance(trees, Tree):
114        trees = [trees]
115    tip_labels = _union_tip_labels(trees)
116
117    lines = ["#NEXUS"]
118    lines.append("BEGIN TAXA;")
119    lines.append(f"  DIMENSIONS NTAX={len(tip_labels)};")
120    lines.append("  TAXLABELS " + " ".join(_quote_label(n) for n in tip_labels) + ";")
121    lines.append("END;")
122    lines.append("BEGIN TREES;")
123    # label -> translate id; a dict makes the per-tip ``_ref_label`` lookup O(1)
124    # instead of a linear scan through the translate table on every node.
125    trans = {n: str(i + 1) for i, n in enumerate(tip_labels)}
126    if trans:
127        lines.append(
128            "  TRANSLATE "
129            + ", ".join(f"{num} {_quote_label(n)}" for n, num in trans.items())
130            + ";"
131        )
132    for i, t in enumerate(trees):
133        label = title if len(trees) == 1 else f"{title}_{i + 1}"
134        lines.append(f"  TREE {label} = [&R] " + _write_ref(t, trans) + ";")
135    lines.append("END;")
136    return "\n".join(lines)

def write_phylip(tree, header: bool = True) -> str: 
58def write_phylip(tree, header: bool = True) -> str:
59    """Write a tree as PHYLIP text (optionally with a ``<ntax> <ntrees>`` header)."""
60    if isinstance(tree, Tree):
61        trees = [tree]
62    else:
63        trees = list(tree)
64    nwk = "\n".join(write_newick(t) for t in trees)
65    ntax = tree.nleaves if isinstance(tree, Tree) else trees[0].nleaves
66    if header:
67        return f"{ntax} {len(trees)}\n{nwk}\n"
68    return nwk + "\n"

Write a tree as PHYLIP text (optionally with a <ntax> <ntrees> header).

def write_phyloxml( tree: Tree, rooted: bool = True, name: str | None = None, properties: list[str] | None = None) -> str: 
105def write_phyloxml(
106    tree: Tree,
107    rooted: bool = True,
108    name: str | None = None,
109    properties: list[str] | None = None,
110) -> str:
111    """Write a Tree as a PhyloXML document string."""
112    phylo = ET.Element("phylogeny")
113    phylo.set("rooted", "true" if rooted else "false")
114    if name:
115        phylo.set("name", name)
116    phylo.append(_clade_elem(tree, properties))
117
118    root = ET.Element("phyloxml")
119    root.append(phylo)
120    # ``ET.indent`` recurses in the stdlib, so it would overflow Python's
121    # recursion limit on a very deep tree.  Use the same formatting produced by
122    # ``ET.indent`` but computed iteratively.
123    _indent(root)
124    return ET.tostring(root, encoding="unicode") + "\n"
